x-research-tools.description: Offline development utility, separate from the whatsapp-cli control API; no HTTP route. BZc still decodes all 110 Message fields. Existing offline descriptor-inspection command; no HTTP route or runtime verification capability. APK 37.71 BWE fields: userJidString=1 (string), verified=2 (bool), verifiedIdentityKey=3 (bytes), actionSeq=4 (int64); BT5 verified=1 (bool), actionSeq=2 (int64). BZb ProtocolMessage markAsVerifiedAction=32 is nested under BZc Message protocolMessage=12. These are recovered schema facts, not a served endpoint or implemented receive policy. Inbound action application is companion-only, requires LID/non-self target, 32-byte key, all field presence and a strictly newer sequence >=1; local metadata writing rechecks identity under lock. Complete serialization, UI triggers and client verification implementation remain unfinished. Evidence: docs/protocol/peer-identity.md. Since 2026-10-13 names are paired by following the newMessageInfo objects array through static helper bodies read from the same APK (the retained-proto-fields simulator), not by literal order; a class that cannot be followed is refused naming the call, and --literal-order prints the old method-order pairing labelled unverified. Not yet run against an APK: tested on retained 2.26.37.71 bodies and synthetic DEX-method input only. Helper bodies are matched on the call's checked full descriptor; an APK scan failure is reported on stderr rather than as an absent method.

Offline development utility, separate from the whatsapp-cli control API; no HTTP route, no APK needed. Reads a committed research disassembly (docs/protocol/apk/**.txt) and follows the straight-line code that builds a protobuf-lite dynamicMethod's newMessageInfo objects array: registers, new-array, aput-object, and static helpers whose bodies are retained from the same APK, matched by the file's SHA-256 header and the call's full descriptor (a shorty-only call is not followed; disagreeing retained copies make the call count as not retained, so the class is refused). The packed-switch fans out; exactly one newMessageInfo call site and exactly one reaching case are required. Every slot must be written once with a field name or class/verifier object, the leading slots must be exactly the descriptor's presence-word count of bitFieldN_ names, and the name count must equal the decoded descriptor's; an array escaping into another array or a field, an instruction rendered without its destination register and an unknown opcode all refuse. Refusals go to stderr naming the reason, including the helper whose body is not retained. --helpers sets the directory searched for helper bodies (default: the bundle directory's parent, only when that is docs/protocol/apk; otherwise --helpers is required). Symlinks are not followed. --literal-order also prints, under a header marked LITERAL ORDER, unverified, the apk-proto-fields method-order pairing for a refused class. APK 2.26.37.71 retained files decode exactly for BZc Message (110), BZD ImageMessage (29), BZB DocumentMessage (21), BZE VideoMessage (30), BZ0 AudioMessage (16), BZK Conversation (59), BY9 PreKeySignalMessage (8), GsB ADVDeviceIdentity (5), 6tK, BSo and BP2 (BSp is literal-order only: its helper call is retained as a shorty); literal order is refuted for BZB, where helper Ayp.A1K writes fileSha256_ at objects[4]. BZc gives pinInChatMessage=63; the BVD PinInChatMessage descriptor is not retained, so pin sending is not implemented. Evidence: docs/protocol/apk-analysis.md#field-numbers-from-retained-bundles-retained-proto-fields-2026-10-13.

info.title: WaRustAPI control API
info.description: This document describes every operation of the whatsapp-api library and whatsapp-cli. The x-transport field indicates whether an operation is served by whatsapp-cli serve over HTTP today or invoked through the CLI. The x-cli field gives the exact command. The x-library field names the Rust entry points behind each operation (crate path form); the whatsapp-cli test `openapi_library_symbols_exist` verifies they exist. The x-live field marks operations that contact WhatsApp servers and require explicit authorization via --allow-live-request. The HTTP control plane has no authentication and binds to loopback only. Feature-boundary correction (2026-11-04): library presence::held_tctoken requires experimental-signal-crypto as well as the presence module's experimental-noise/experimental-transport features, because PN/LID lookup uses the encrypted inbox. Reduced Noise/transport builds omit this helper instead of silently dropping its lookup. No HTTP route or full-client wire behavior changes.

Conflict.description: Resource already exists, is reserved, or operation cannot proceed due to state conflict

Blocked.description: Operation blocked by server refusal, cooldown or preserved state

UsyncRefusalFailure.description: Fixed local numeric parse failure; no raw values.

code.description: Signed Java integer; absent attribute uses0 for outer usync_refusal, -1 for contact_protocol_refusal; malformed present is null.

backoff_millis.description: Signed wrapping seconds*1000 capped above. Absent=-1 for outer usync_refusal, 3600000 for contact_protocol_refusal; invalid present=null. A relative parsed value, not an enforced wait.

ContactProjection.description: Local single-contact projection result. Applied does not imply on-WhatsApp or complete native protocol success. Rejected projection preserves data and is not account absence or a retry permit.

TokenIssueCompletion.description: Local selected direct-user timestamp persistence effect of a correlated token result, not delivery, effective expiry or a retry permit.

ActionDeferReason.description: Local pre-write action deferral, distinct from server refusal or uncertain delivery. Missing contact-check correlation holds historical queued requests; it is not a retry permit.

HistoryNoticeMetadata.description: History-notice metadata model returned by the pure decoder and carried on the received GroupHistoryNotice event. It is not a standalone HTTP response. Returns null for another message type, a metadata model for a supported notice, or a fixed redacted local error. No receiver addresses or opaque context/bot contents are retained. Positive count/window timestamp mirror APK 2.26.37.71 DA8.CF4. Timestamp units remain unknown. This helper does not authenticate or dispatch a notice.

message_count.description: Positive signed int64 count from BX5 field 3.

oldest_window_timestamp.description: Positive raw signed int64 window timestamp, BX5 field 2; unit unknown.

oldest_bundle_timestamp.description: Optional raw signed int64 bundle timestamp, BX5 field 5; unit and validity policy untraced.

receiver_count.description: Number of supported primary PN/LID history receivers; positive and locally limited to 1024.

non_receiver_count.description: Number of supported primary PN/LID non-history receivers; locally limited to 1024.

context_present.description: Opaque BV6 field 1 is present; its contents are not returned or validated.

bot_metadata_present.description: Opaque BV6 field 3 is present; its contents are not returned or validated.

PhoneNumber.description: Structured phone number with country code and national components

Jid.description: WhatsApp JID (Jabber ID) in form username@s.whatsapp.net for direct chats or username@g.us for groups

RequestId.description: Caller-supplied idempotency key; repeating the same request_id returns the saved outcome locally and never resends

Ok.description: Successful local-only mutation with no richer result

ActionStatus.description: Status of a queued action transmission. `sent` means reserved for a socket write (marked before the write so a cut never resends it); whether it reached the socket is unknown until `ok`/`error` arrives.

kind.description: Kind of saved observation; does not grant native receipt_user membership.

server.description: Serialized Server enum, not wire domain text.

contact.description: Actual serialized ContactId/Jid object; CLI input JID strings use the separate Jid schema.

device.description: Device attribution where applicable; null for a server ACK. Direct participant-qualified receipts preserve this actual actor only when its user matches the saved direct chat and its device belongs to the immutable original target snapshot. Authenticated PN/LID association may join namespaces; historical target gaps are not filled from current membership.

server_timestamp.description: Parsed server ACK or supported receipt time in milliseconds, separate from local observed_at. APK 37.71 signed BMP-decimal parsing and wrapping multiplication apply. Success ACK missing/invalid t defaults to zero (1Qy.A02); direct/group receipt facts retain valid supplied root t, including signed zero/negative/wrapped values, and omit missing/nontext/invalid time (Cmk.A03/0Gv.A01). Receipt facts preserve the first observation per kind/device; later earliest-positive device-row times can differ. Historical facts remain unmodified. This is evidence, not clock authority, native receipt_user admission or completed delivery. Offline tested; qualifying live receipt projection unverified. Offline aggregated message_id receipt facts instead require each entry t via strict Java-decimal parsing; missing/invalid input refuses the entire batch. Valid signed/wrapped values remain supplied evidence; no wall-clock fallback is used for this branch. Participants-key multi-target receipts instead apply root status and each target time; absent entry t uses one confirmed/local receipt-parser clock default. Present malformed/overflow time refuses the entire batch, and missing/invalid optional JIDs skip before time parsing. Native NTP preference is unported; this fallback can differ from the APK when NTP is active. It is not new clock authority.

code.description: Signed ACK error code where present. New ACK facts preserve the admitted Java i32 value including Unicode digits; historical unsigned-u32 values remain readable in this wider storage type. A code alone grants no retry or account-policy authority.

DeliveryFact.description: Actual serialized durable DeliveryFact; inspect using status.

progress.description: Local attempt progress; delivery evidence is stored separately in facts.

facts.description: Durable facts in local observation order. ServerAccepted is not handset delivery or read.

SendStatus.description: Actual serialized SendStatus returned by CLI status. No HTTP message-status route is served.

wire_id.description: Client-generated wire ID when persisted; null while profile format is unknown.

accepted_at.description: Local durable enqueue time, Unix milliseconds; not server acceptance.

SendTicket.description: Actual serialized ticket for a durable local send intent.

to.description: Direct recipient: E.164 digits, a `…@s.whatsapp.net` JID, or a `…@lid` JID. Omit when `group` is set. The LID form exists because a LID-addressed chat encrypts under a LID Signal address, which needs to be testable outside a group fan-out.

group.description: Group chat JID (`…@g.us`) for a sender-key fan-out send. Mutually exclusive with `to`. lab-transport sends group text, replies and reactions only and refuses group image/voice_note/view_once JSON; outbox-send also accepts uploaded group image/voice_note (2026-10-13: previously the shared reader refused group media, so the documented outbox-send group media path was unreachable from the CLI). lab-transport resolves the membership with a `w:g2` info query, the members' devices with `usync devices`, then addresses every device individually.

fresh_sessions.description: Discard the saved Signal session with each recipient device and establish a new one from a fresh prekey bundle, keeping the pinned peer identity (a changed identity is still refused). Applies to both the direct and the group fan-out path. Only legitimate with positive evidence that the peer never received what was encrypted under the old session.

skdm_delivery.description: Group send only: how the sender key is distributed. `participants` (default) puts one `<enc>` per device inside the group stanza's `<participants>`; `direct` sends one ordinary direct message per device carrying the distribution, before the group stanza, and omits `<participants>` entirely. Both are real — `includeSenderKeysInMessage` is a per-send flag in SendE2EMessageJob and SendLiveLocationKeyJob distributes keys entirely out of band.

image.description: Path to a PNG image file to send

voice_note.description: Path to an Ogg/Opus audio file to send as a voice note

view_once.description: If true, image is sent as view-once (disappears after one viewing)

status.description: Post a status instead of sending to a chat; mutually exclusive with `to` and `group`

quote.description: Reply to, or react to, an existing message in the chat named by `group` or `to`. lab-transport handles group replies (with optional quoted_text) and group reactions, and refuses any direct-chat quote. outbox-send (normal outbox) accepts replies only, in groups and (2026-10-13) direct chats, with exactly one of text, image or voice_note, and refuses reactions and quoted_text before any store access or send-path claim: a participant naming one of our identities quotes our outgoing message; any other names the incoming author, which in a direct chat must be the contact itself in the same form as `to`. quotedMessage is built from the saved parent, never a caller preview.

document.description: Path to a document file (1 byte to 8 MiB) to upload and send as DocumentMessage (Message field 7; 2.26.37.71 BZ6 fields 2-11, no url). Encrypted with the WhatsApp Document Keys domain, uploaded to /mms/document, stanza enc mediatype=document. File name from the path; MIME type from the extension (pdf, txt, csv, zip, json, docx, xlsx) else application/octet-stream. Exclusive with text, image and voice_note; not for status posts or comparison group sends.

video.description: Path to an MP4 (at most 8 MiB) to upload and send as VideoMessage (Message field 9; 2.26.37.71 BZE fields url 1, mimetype 2, fileSha256 3, fileLength 4, seconds 5, mediaKey 6, height 9, width 10, fileEncSha256 11, directPath 13, mediaKeyTimestamp 14). Duration and size are read from moov/mvhd and the first video trak/tkhd. Encrypted with the WhatsApp Video Keys domain, uploaded to /mms/video, stanza mediatype=video. No thumbnail or caption. Exclusive with text, image, voice_note and document.

MessageRequest.description: Private JSON message request for outbox-send or lab-transport --message. Exactly one target: `to` (direct), `group` (sender-key fan-out) or `status` (a status post). Repeating the same request_id returns the saved outcome locally and never resends.

state.description: Current state of the queued entry

OutboxEntry.description: An entry in the durable outbox queue awaiting transmission

settlement_sequence.description: Local durable monotonic receive order, assigned atomically with a newly correlated terminal IQ reply. Null for unsettled or legacy unknown-order rows; never derived from random IDs or timestamps. Sequenced contact/group/blocklist projection replay uses oldest-first order across relevant kinds. Legacy unsequenced replies remain inspectable and are excluded from that automatic projection path without changing markers or send reservations. This local order does not prove server snapshot freshness or native generation admission.

kind.description: Type of action (block, report, lookup, etc.)

error_code.description: Server error code if action failed

error_text.description: Server error message if action failed

deferred_reason.description: Optional last local reservation deferral; cleared when reserved. Omitted when absent.

token_issue_completion.description: Optional trusted-contact result effect saved atomically with settlement; omitted for legacy/unrelated/unsuccessful actions. No raw user/time.

contact_projection.description: Optional local contact-status projection result, distinct from outer IQ status. Saved atomically with status/once-only marker; omitted for legacy/unrelated/not-yet-projected rows. No raw phone/time.

about_refusal.description: Optional typed About outer-error diagnostic. Ordered direct-child Java Integer codes before first malformed present code. Legacy absence unknown; no backfill or retry authority. Generic error_code remains compatibility u16.

contact_protocol_refusal.description: Optional contact-protocol error inside an owned outer usync result for requested contact protocol. Backoff parsed before code; absent wait is3600000ms and code-1. Separate from outer status, per-user type and outer-IQ refusal. Legacy absence is unknown; no backfill, wait enforcement or retry authorization.

usync_refusal.description: Optional parsed usync outer-IQ error metadata saved at settlement. Legacy absence means unknown/unparsed, not no wait. Inspection only; not an enforced absolute deadline or retry permit.

ActionOutcome.description: Outcome of a one-shot queued action. Settlement receive order is a local journal property, not a server field. Session-specific pending group recovery also uses the sequenced order across group action kinds; unknown-order legacy pending replies remain preserved without projection, marker consumption or resend. Evidence and legacy limitations: docs/protocol/action-settlement-ordering.md.

status.description: Durable receipt transmission outcome. An acknowledged retry is not confirmation of replacement-message delivery.

message_id.description: Wire message ID referenced by the queued receipt; no recipient or message content is included.

automatic.description: True for a newly automatic read intent, false for an explicit read, null for legacy/other unknown provenance. No provenance is fabricated for historical rows.

deferred_reason.description: Fixed reason a pending automatic direct read is retained without reservation after a known disabled server preference. Read-self remains unported. Cleared on eligible reservation or explicit promotion; no automatic reset of an uncertain send.

ReceiptOutcome.description: Outcome of a queued read, played or automatic once-only retry receipt transmission. Native-derived negative privacy guard applies only to newly automatic direct reads at queue and reservation; explicit reads and existing group behavior remain unchanged. Pending deferred work is retained under its original selector. Full read-self/companion/contact policy remains unported; no fresh live validation. Evidence docs/protocol/read-receipt-policy-current.md.

state.description: Saved attempt state name exactly as RegistrationState::name() prints it

blocked_reason.description: Reason for account block if state is blocked. Since 2026-10-13 a saved ServerRefused may carry not_before: the earliest time another request of the refused kind may be sent, the longest sms_wait, voice_wait or email_otp_wait of a refusal without retry_after. The one-shot diagnostics and corrections, resume-email-challenge and the exist probe enforce it. Absent in older records and when the refusal carried no wait.

retry_after_seconds.description: Seconds to wait before retrying if in cooling_down state

answer_not_before_unix_ms.description: Optional --json step diagnostic for PIN actions: maximum saved guessing and generic PIN deadline, in Unix milliseconds. The saved attempt retains the underlying challenge fields. A later answer must still use the current handle and explicit live authorization.

RegistrationStep.description: Snapshot of the current registration state and next actions

generation.description: Attempt generation number for state recovery

phone.description: Phone number in masked format (+1 <10 digits>)

RegistrationAttempt.description: Complete registration attempt with full state history

token.description: Base64-encoded phone-bound registration token derived from APK comparison material

signed_pre_key_id.description: Signed pre-key ID (must fit in 24 bits)

facebook_device_id.description: Facebook device identifier; null means generate once and persist

experiment_id.description: Experiment identifier; null means generate once and persist

access_session_id.description: Access session identifier; null means generate once and persist

recovery_token.description: Account recovery token; null means generate once and persist

backup_token.description: Backup recovery token; null means generate once and persist

fields.description: Request field templates organized by step (exist, code, register, security) with optional _bytes variants for encoded versions. Configured fields.code_bytes.client_metrics for ordinary SMS/voice code requests must be a JSON object; attempts is refreshed from complete saved preparation history (not delivery count), preserving other properties. Malformed metrics or incomplete history refuse before I/O. No metrics field is injected when absent; email_otp and explicit diagnostic overrides keep their existing behavior. Offline verified; delivery improvement is unverified.

body_mode.description: HTTP body encoding mode: clear_form (plaintext form), enc (encrypted), or enc_empty_h (encrypted with empty hash)

connect_timeout_ms.description: TCP connection timeout in milliseconds (must be <= timeout_ms)

max_response_bytes.description: Maximum response body size in bytes

max_attempts.description: Maximum consecutive reconnection attempts (0 disables reconnection). The count resets only after an activated connection stayed up for at least max_delay_ms, or on an explicit connect; a server that activates and then drops at once still exhausts it (client policy, not an APK value).

max_delay_ms.description: Maximum backoff delay in milliseconds; also the minimum activated-connection lifetime that resets the attempt count

action_delay_ms.description: Monotonic pacing gap after each successful generic queued-action write within a drain. The connection reserves one eligible action only when due and waits in select, allowing incoming replies/stop/deadlines between sends; no batch sleep. Existing activation/heartbeat triggers keep a maximum sixteen-action drain budget, and repeated triggers do not stack/reset an active drain. A new drain's first action is immediate; this is not a global rate limit across all stanza families. Readiness means authenticated activation, not actionqueue flush. Startup/heartbeat IQs may precede queued generic actions. Socket-write completion itself still awaits; full app-state flight ownership remains unported. See docs/protocol/app-state-connection-flight-design.md.

mark_read.description: During a messaging session (`listen`), send a read receipt for every incoming direct or group message with readable content (Message fields 1, 3, 6, 7, 8, 9, 26 or 66) that decrypts. Sender-key distributions, protocol messages and reactions get none. Each receipt goes through the same durable, once-only queue as `mark-read`. Applies to `listen` and to `lab-transport --receive`. Off by default: the official client marks messages read when a chat is on screen, which this client cannot infer. Applies to eligible authenticated duplicates on redelivery too, including offline recovery; durable read markers prevent repetitions after uncertain writes or ACKs. Default true since 2026-11-02 (was false).

identity_changes.description: Incoming remote prekey trust policy for listen and lab receive. pinned refuses changed saved identities. apk_authenticated permits replacement only after nested message authentication, atomically archiving the prior pin/session and emitting IdentityChanged with the inbox commit. It does not establish human verification. Own-device messages remain pinned. Outgoing bundle replacement has a separate opt-in outgoing_identity_changes; uncertain sends never replay.

outgoing_identity_changes.description: Independent outgoing remote directory-bundle policy for the normal comparison outbox. Pinned suspends changed identities. Apk_authenticated requires a valid signed device key received through authenticated Noise, derives a fresh peer session, archives prior pin/session with signed_directory_bundle provenance and emits IdentityChanged atomically with the original send reservation. Own-account identities remain pinned. It is not human verification. Incoming identity_changes does not enable this. Unknown/refused queries and uncertain sends never resume. Repeating the original outbox-send JSON may resolve an identity-suspended intent using its saved reply; no new query or intent ID is created. General listen --send-outbox does not select suspended intents. Suspensions without an observed pin snapshot cannot resume, and stale replies cannot roll a newer current peer pin back. This setting applies to direct and ordinary group normal-outbox bundles actually fetched by their workflows. Group replacements archive signed-directory provenance atomically with the original fanout/send reservation and rotate exposed sender-key generations. Own identities remain pinned. A changed primary with companions whose saved authority used its old pin blocks as companion_authority_changed. Group preparation resume and companion reconciliation remain unfinished; no marker is reset and cached sessions do not trigger unsolicited directory refreshes.

profile.description: Optional profile queued when registration completes (2026-11-01), the way the official setup flow asks for a name right after verification: push_name queues the pushNameSetting app-state record and the display-name presence (0y0 case 3), about queues the About text. The next session (listen) transmits them; nothing is sent during registration. The name is validated before any request.

LabRegistrationConfig.description: Lab registration configuration template. The default recipe (body_mode enc_empty_h, client.user_agent 'WhatsApp/2.26.37.70 Android/unknown Device/unknown-unknown', and recommended code fields) is now provided by lab-signup template (GET /v1/signup/template). The token must be derived from 2.26.37.70 APK material; see docs/protocol/registration-lab.md for details.

reason.description: Server failure reason (e.g., BadParam, BadToken, TooManyAllMethods, Incorrect, Blocked, Challenge)

invalid_parameter.description: Name of invalid parameter if reason is BadParam

retry_after_seconds.description: Seconds to wait before retrying if rate-limited

guess_wait_seconds.description: Separate server security-code guessing delay in seconds (APK 2.26.43.72 KotlinRegistrationBridge.A07/A0B, VerifyPhoneNumber.A11, IBz.run). Parsed by the library and included in response diagnostics. Saved refused responses retain the longest applicable wait; this does not enable unsupported PIN retries or replace the ordinary OTP mismatch retry_after timer.

sms_wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for SMS code delivery

voice_wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for voice call code delivery

body_shape.description: Top-level JSON field names and value types (null/bool/number/string/array/object) from the raw response body; no values. Present on all parsed responses so unknown or extra server fields are visible in diagnostics.

custom_block_screen_shape.description: Field names and JSON value types from the custom_block_screen object, when present (Blocked responses). No values. APK KotlinRegistrationBridge.A0O stores this as a generic Map; fields are server-defined. Capped at 32 entries.

RegistrationReply.description: Redacted server reply for registration requests

invalid_parameter.description: Name of invalid parameter if applicable

guess_wait_seconds.description: Optional security-code guessing wait, in seconds, reported independently of retry_after_seconds; no additional request is authorized.

voice_wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for voice call

email_otp_eligible.description: Whether account is eligible for email OTP

wa_old_eligible.description: Whether account is eligible for old WhatsApp recovery

masked_email.description: Masked email address associated with account

ExistProbe.description: Existence probe result with account recovery options

RequestPreview.description: Redacted request plan for lab-signup preview

ConsentSelectors.description: Selectors for consent options in registration flow

EndpointFields.description: Dynamic endpoint request fields derived from server requirements

store.description: Path to the protocol database file

config.description: Path to private request configuration file

key_env.description: Environment variable name holding the master key

AccountProfile.description: Named account profile with database and configuration paths

journal_head.description: Current position in the durable event journal

StoreInspection.description: Summary of protocol database state and structure

hex.description: Hexadecimal representation of the 256-bit master key (64 hex characters)

MasterKey.description: Master encryption key (secret; stdout only). Store securely in a secret manager.

Contact.description: Address book contact with WhatsApp verification status

group_type.description: Complete-reply child classification in APK 37.71 ADs.A01 precedence order. Historical rows/local stubs are null, not inferred ordinary.

linked_parent.description: Supported non-device concrete group JID from the first linked_parent child; absent/invalid identities remain null independently of classification.

subject_time.description: Stored s_t wire value; separate notification version cache is not inferred.

Group.description: Actual group list --json snapshot shape. New optional classification fields default to null when reading historical rows.

revoked.description: Whether the invite link has been revoked

expected_timestamp.description: Server expected_ts or a newer authenticated known-companion ADV expectation; never the verified list timestamp. A signed normal response below it retains pending sync; reaching it clears the old expectation. APK 37.71 0bN.A05 / Lcr.A00.

companions_verified.description: Signed account baseline authority; individually ADV-added entries are separately identified by adv_added_devices. Current primary-key binding remains a separate check.

fetched_at.description: Local saved ingest time in Unix milliseconds.

adv_added_devices.description: Local provenance: actual devices added by authenticated individually signed ADV, awaiting signed-list address/index confirmation. Historical rows default empty. Not a server wire field.

pending_removed_devices.description: Namespace-local removals recorded by successful signed reconciliation. Null is unknown legacy state; [] is known empty. Authenticated returned devices clear markers. Unsigned ingestion does not initialize or clear this metadata. No key cleanup/reset is implied; not a server field.

DeviceList.description: Actual CLI saved historical list schema. The private optional verified_primary_key_fingerprint is stored by the library but omitted from CLI output; old rows remain unbound. No served HTTP handler.

id.description: Opaque selector: SHA-256 hex of the encrypted inbox record key received:{chat}:{message id} (or received-own:...); pass it to media-open or media-save.

kind.description: Attachment kind. Ordinary stickers are URL-bearing WebP; video and video notes URL-bearing MP4. CLI text output prints the variant names Image, VoiceNote, Sticker, Video, VideoNote and Document. Documents use their distinct Document Keys domain and explicit media-save output; live incoming documents remain unverified. View-once content never appears here.

bytes.description: Advertised plaintext length from the attachment descriptor (not verified until download).

MediaItem.description: Redacted ordinary incoming attachment selector (media-list). Corrected 2026-10-13: earlier versions of this schema listed mime, downloaded and opened fields and a view_once_image kind that the list never produced.

KeepInChatChange.description: Inner event.MessageUpdated.change.KeepInChat data in full CLI EventEnvelope JSON. Received facts only; no keep permission, ordering application or expiry enforcement. Legacy records omit the optional fields.

by.description: Serialized acting DeviceAddress; contact is a ContactId wrapping its Jid object.

sender_timestamp.description: BV3.timestampMs field 3 in milliseconds. Signed wire value; absent differs from explicit zero. Not stanza time or local observation time.

update_id.description: Keep/unkeep envelope ID. MessageUpdate.key.id remains the original target. Unsupported, absent or historical IDs are unknown.

kind.description: Event type (message, receipt, action, etc.). group_history_notice is a typed received control notice; it is not counted as a human reply or completed history transfer.

payload.description: Event-specific data. A GroupHistoryNotice event carries key, metadata (HistoryNoticeMetadata), server_timestamp and observed_at. The enum serialization is received-only; MessageContent/SendRequest cannot deserialize this event as outgoing content. KeepInChat enum data additionally carries by, kept and optional sender_timestamp (signed int64 milliseconds) and update_id (supported wire MessageId string). The received change is event.MessageUpdated.change.KeepInChat in full CLI EventEnvelope JSON; MessageUpdate.key.id is the target, not update_id. Optional fields are omitted for historical or unavailable metadata.

Event.description: Entry in the durable event journal

acked.description: Whether the batch has been acknowledged

EventBatch.description: Batch of events from the journal

unsent.description: Generated one-time prekeys never included in a reserved upload batch (APK sent_to_server = 0).

uncertain.description: One-time prekeys in a reserved batch whose outcome is unknown; they are never re-sent.

uploaded.description: One-time prekeys in a batch the server acknowledged (APK sent_to_server = 1).

batches.description: Reserved upload batches counted by status: outcome_unknown, server_acknowledged or refused.

kem_local.description: Local ML-KEM-1024 prekey inventory used by incoming hybrid bootstrap. Enabled comparison SET uploads can generate/upload rows; current native ADD/replenishment parity remains incomplete.

kem_last_resort.description: Of kem_local, rows marked as native last-resort keys; these are retained after successful use (APK 2.26.37.71 0kh.BWa deletes only last_resort_key = 0).

pq_low_acknowledged_batches.description: Historical acknowledged upload batches recording pq_list/@count_low=true. Not current server demand; old batches without the field stay unknown and do not count. No automatic PQ follow-up is implied.

upload_held_after_refusal.description: A saved refused upload holds all new automatic upload reservations while native retry/backoff/regeneration policy remains unported. No cooldown or safe retry time is inferred. Historical refusals also hold; no automatic reset.

PrekeyStatus.description: Redacted one-time and KEM prekey inventory and upload-batch status, as emitted by `prekeys --json`. No key material is returned.

hash.description: Server hash of the block list for change detection

refresh_queued.description: Whether a block list refresh has been queued

BlockList.description: Local copy of the server block list

BanAppealResult.description: Result of ban appeal submission via ACS GraphQL

CapabilityMatrix.description: Capability matrix of the protocol profile: features, version constraints, supported operations

ProtocolProfile.description: Protocol profile with evidence labels and derivation provenance

WireProfile.description: Comparison APK wire protocol profile: message formats, header layouts, serialization modes

Health.description: Control plane server health and version information

ServiceIndex.description: Index of available services and their endpoints

SessionSummary.description: Summary statistics from a live session

received.description: Whether the message was received by the other account

PairCheckResult.description: Result of a two-account pair check (lab-pair)

skipped.description: Number of messages skipped or unable to decrypt

kinds.description: Count of decrypted messages by kind

InboxSummary.description: Summary of inbox decryption results from lab-inbox

note.description: Explanation that transmission occurs in a live session

QueuedAck.description: Acknowledgment that an operation has been durably queued for transmission by a session

profile_path.description: Path to the created account profile file

store.description: Path to the protocol database file

config.description: Path to the private request configuration file

master_key_path.description: Path to the saved master key (file mode 0600)

key_env.description: Environment variable name to set with the master key

next_steps.description: Recommended next operations to complete onboarding

AccountCreated.description: Result of successful account onboarding. Token, key and phone are never printed; files are created with permissions 0600 (profile, config) and 0700 (directories).

store.description: Path to the protocol database file

locked.description: True if the master key environment variable is not set

key_env.description: Environment variable name holding the master key

registration_state.description: Saved registration attempt state (unregistered, preparing, challenge_pending, needs_user_action, email_challenge_required, email_code_pending, verifying, outcome_unknown, registered, cooling_down, blocked) or none when no attempt exists

registered.description: True if the account is registered with WhatsApp

last_authenticated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of last successful authentication

login_checkpoint.description: Last primary-login checkpoint: success, refused, outcome_unknown, or none

appeal_token_saved.description: True if a ban appeal token is persisted

outbox_pending.description: Logical entries needing work (Queued, Prepared, RetryScheduled), excluding retained Cancelled/Failed/InFlight history. Not a count of currently sendable reservations.

actions_queued.description: Number of chat actions queued (blocks, reports, privacy settings)

AccountStatus.description: Status summary of a registered account

token.description: Base64-encoded phone-bound registration token (secret; redacted in logs)

logo_entry.description: Internal APK material entry identifier for logo (debug only)

signature_entry.description: Internal APK material entry identifier for signature (debug only)

DerivedToken.description: Derived registration token from APK material. Token is base64-encoded and phone-bound; store it securely.

matches.description: True if the token in the config matches the derived token; false otherwise

TokenVerification.description: Verification result comparing a saved token to freshly derived material. Token value is never printed; only the match status is reported.

AppStatePatchRequest.description: Outgoing w:sync:app:state patch request, exposed through durable contact/name publication. Native producer shape is reanchored to APK 2.26.43.72 EfK/EdY in docs/protocol/app-state-versioned-fetch.md; historical 400/409 observations are documented separately. Preparation, original wire and frozen baseline commit atomically; reservation revalidates preparation and explicit server backoff. Accepted replies promote only their authenticated sequential transition. Legacy preparation missing logical-index metadata may acquire it only by verifying its unchanged original patch against a current authenticated baseline and matching every frozen collection/version/hash/wire-MAC field; supplied metadata must match too. Missing current provenance or entire preparation still refuses. No request rebuild, key change or retry is introduced; see docs/protocol/app-state-patch-atomicity.md. Conflict catch-up resolves patch and record key IDs separately from already-held account keys in one transaction; absent keys or invalid MACs refuse without partial state. Full native action projection, scheduling and recovery remain incomplete. See docs/protocol/app-state-catchup-atomicity.md. No HTTP route is served.

collection.description: Collection name (LX/0oP.A03, confirmed). This low-level builder takes the collection from its caller; supported contact/name publication selects its evidence-backed action collection.

order.description: 1 for critical_unblock_low, 0 otherwise (inferred from the CSe.A01 branch; the attribute's meaning was not traced).

version.description: Held collection version on the outer collection element, not the patch's post-update version. Omitted when absent. The authenticated patch transition advances the held version by one; outgoing SyncdPatch omits its internal version field.

return_snapshot.description: Emitted only when requested and the held version is absent or zero, matching the pinned native producer.

patch.description: SyncdPatch wire bytes from CollectionState::build_patch: mutations, snapshotMac, patchMac and nested keyId; no internal version on the outgoing write.

TextStyle.description: Colour and font of a styled full-screen text status, decoded from extendedTextMessage (LX/BZF descriptor, confirmed). All fields absent for an ordinary chat message. Carried on MessageContent::Text in the event journal.

background_argb.description: backgroundArgb, field 8, FIXED32 on the wire (unsigned, 4 bytes little-endian — NOT a varint int32). ARGB with alpha most significant.

text_argb.description: textArgb, field 7, FIXED32 on the wire. ARGB with alpha most significant.

font.description: font, field 9. Enum LX/C44 covers exactly wire values 0..=8; anything else is dropped rather than mapped.

audience.description: Identities allowed to see it (phone-number or LID form). Explicit because a status has no membership list and this client does not sync the account's status privacy list — this is WhatsApp's "share with only…".

background.description: Background colour as ARGB hex, with or without a leading #

text_color.description: Text colour as ARGB hex, with or without a leading #

StatusPost.description: A text or image status. Posted through the same sender-key fan-out as a group message, addressed to status@broadcast, with no addressing_mode and no phash (neither is observed on an incoming status). With `image` set on the request the picture replaces the text rather than captioning it, and `text` must be empty.

status_id.description: The status we posted, by wire id

kind.description: Delivered (receipt with no type), Read (viewed), Played (video watched or voice heard)

StatusReceipt.description: One viewer's report about one of our statuses. Observed shape: `<receipt from=<viewer> [type]><participants message_id=<status id>/></receipt>` — the status is named by the participants child, not the receipt's own id. Recorded only; this client sends no read receipts of its own.

status_id.description: The status reacted to, by wire id

emoji.description: The emoji; null is a reaction being removed, recorded rather than dropped so a like does not appear to persist forever

StatusLike.description: A like on one of our statuses. A status reaction is an ordinary Message.reactionMessage (field 46) whose key names status@broadcast as the remoteJid — that is what distinguishes it from a chat reaction. In the APK it lands in status_add_on with type = 1, which a trigger counts into status_interactions.reaction_count.

message_id.description: Wire id of the message replied to or reacted to

participant.description: Who sent it. A group message id means nothing without this — the same id from two members is two different messages.

emoji.description: React with this emoji instead of replying; an empty string removes a previous reaction, which is a real operation and not the same as absent

quoted_text.description: The quoted message's own text, carried as quotedMessage. Absent quotes an empty body rather than inventing one. Comparison path only; outbox-send refuses it and copies the saved parent text.

QuotedTarget.description: An existing message to reply to or react to (group, or direct for outbox-send replies). A reply carries `text` and no emoji; a reaction carries an emoji and no body — a reaction with a body, or a reply without one, renders as something else entirely on the recipient.

applied.description: Durable historical application of this original read to a changed-primary classic pin/session. False for old/untracked, unsupported, refused or not applied reads. True is once-only application history, not current key agreement, a human safety-number verification or notification ACK.

force_override_e2ee_state.description: Presence of force_override_e2ee_state child on the correlated selected-user parsed bundle, not root metadata or an attribute. Null until a parsed bundle, including signature-invalid bundles. This is server input inspected offline, not a local switch or complete native admission.

companion_same_key_authority.description: Local known-companion same-key directory authority diagnostic. Null for primary, incomplete or invalid-signature replies. ready for a listed companion requires a unique nonnull device-identity byte body, exact held companion key, current saved membership bound to its primary pin, protected own namespace and no explicit pending teardown. ADV bytes are not parsed on that listed same-key fast return. This diagnostic does not authorize application: pinned policy, metadata, original guards and atomic reply/session/account checks still apply. Changed companion ADV authority is reported separately in companion_changed_key_authority. ready_addition_pending means an already pinned companion is absent from retained membership and its full signed ADV passes independent-primary/E2EE/raw-ID/index/newer signed-time admission. If application policy/metadata/original guards and exact transaction state still permit it, membership plus ADV provenance, pending sync and session are committed together. A same key does not bypass ADV parsing while absent. Index collision, 1024-device overflow or explicit pending teardown refuse. No first-seen pin, invented removal state or canonical PN/LID alias is authorized.

companion_changed_key_authority.description: Local changed-companion directory authority diagnostic. Null for primary, incomplete/invalid-signature replies or when no differing held pin exists. Requires independently pinned primary, current bound device-list baseline, both ADV signatures over the actual directory identity, E2EE/raw-ID baseline and signed Java-long freshness. ready_refresh_pending raises the pending expectation atomically with application, retaining the verified floor and existing device index. ready is not permission to bypass identity policy, original notification guards, unsupported metadata, own identity or exact commit-state checks. First-seen companions, primary/raw-ID replacement and full native admission remain unported. ready_addition_pending means an already pinned companion is absent from retained membership and its full signed ADV passes independent-primary/E2EE/raw-ID/index/newer signed-time admission. If application policy/metadata/original guards and exact transaction state still permit it, membership plus ADV provenance, pending sync and session are committed together. A same key does not bypass ADV parsing while absent. Index collision, 1024-device overflow or explicit pending teardown refuse. No first-seen pin, invented removal state or canonical PN/LID alias is authorized.

The token goes to the new mode-0600 file only, never stdout or logs, and the file is removed on Ctrl-C, SIGTERM or SIGHUP. Clients should use 127.0.0.1 rather than localhost. Default serve remains store-less.

get.summary: Show queued one-shot actions and their outcomes
get.description: Show queued one-shot actions (block list, reports, lookups) and their outcomes (offline, redacted). Includes identity_refresh directory reads queued by authenticated identity notifications. An ok action means a correlated generic result, not verified bundle or adopted identity. Refused/invalid/uncertain reads are retained; offline inspection never transmits a chat or changes a pin/session. For identity_refresh actions only, --show prints a structured redacted snapshot with namespace/device, exact refusal code, signed-bundle validity and current-pin comparison; no raw request, reply, peer address or key is printed. verified_bundle authenticates the fetched signed device key, not adoption or human verification. --show ID --preview-session is an offline cryptographic preview for identity_refresh only. It derives and discards a supported primary or authenticated companion classic session without constructing a chat. Same-key candidates retain held receiving state in the candidate archive; changed keys derive fresh with zero old archives. It never writes a candidate or evaluates native CPB admission. Unsupported attestation, PQ metadata, missing pins, unverified replies and failed companion authority do not derive; a reused held session that does not deserialize or whose remote identity, local identity or registration does not match the pin and saved account reports held_session_inconsistent; application defers with the same reason (row kept, logged), so connection-start recovery never stops on it. Evidence docs/protocol/hybrid-identity-refresh.md#damaged-held-sessions-2026-10-13. Unknown native stored attestation state is not assumed NOT_SET or E2EE. Evidence: docs/protocol/session-refresh-preview.md. Newly queued identity_refresh actions now atomically capture original generation, exact pin fingerprint, exact-device authenticated transition marker and nullable primary-user version. --show prints refresh_guard (matches, untracked, pin_changed, transition_changed, primary_version_changed, generation_changed); markers and fingerprints stay private. Duplicate events keep the original baseline; missing historical snapshots remain untracked. Matching guards do not establish CPB admission or commit authority. --preview-session skips derivation for a known stale guard. Evidence: docs/protocol/identity-refresh-guards.md. For supported selected-device identity_refresh replies, --show additionally inspects non_e2ee_attestation: allowed declared account type, BP2 field-1 closed-enum projection, matching type and signature over APK prefix 06 07 plus the original value bytes. Attestation and signed-key validity remain separate from current-pin agreement, refresh guards and native CPB admission. Raw values/signatures and unknown server strings are never printed. get.summary: Event kinds after a consumer's acknowledged cursor (offline, redacted)
get.description: The `events --summary --json` form: one object with the consumer name, the acknowledged cursor the batch starts after (after_cursor), the cursor that would acknowledge it (ack_cursor), has_more, and the event kinds in journal order (for example new_message, receipt_updated, message_deleted). No message content, chat, sender or message ID. Reading never acknowledges, so repeating it answers the same batch; acknowledging stays CLI-only (`events --ack`). Without --json the CLI prints one `event: <kind>` line per event and the counts on stderr. A consumer whose cursor precedes trimmed events (for example a name never used before a trim) is refused: the CLI reports the expired cursor, HTTP answers 409 cursor_expired naming the last trimmed cursor (events through it were removed; the first retained event is the next cursor). HTTP (2026-10-13): served read-only by `whatsapp-cli serve --store-routes --token-file <new path>` (experimental-transport build), loopback only, with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; the store is opened per request with the serve process's --store/--account/--key-env, so it answers 503 store_unavailable only while another command (for example listen) holds the store, and 500 store_read_failed for any other read failure; a command starting during a request can fail to open the store and must be rerun. HEAD is also served. Disabled store routes answer 404 store_routes_disabled; a missing or wrong token 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer. Over HTTP the limit is fixed at the CLI default (50) and the only accepted query is exactly consumer=<name>, unencoded, ASCII alphanumerics and -_.: only, at most 64 bytes (the library ConsumerId bound); a missing, renamed, repeated, empty, percent-encoded or additional parameter (including limit) answers 400 before the store opens. A consumer name using other printable characters, which the CLI accepts, cannot be queried over HTTP. The other parameters listed here are CLI flags; over HTTP the store comes from the serve process.

post.summary: Decrypt captured direct replies locally, without network I/O
post.description: Decrypt authenticated incoming records locally. The operation is offline. Saved-payload inspection labels Message field 102 as message-history-notice and shows only its nested field numbers, grounded in APK 2.26.37.71 BZc/BV6.dynamicMethod. Supported history-notice metadata is validated using BX5 and DA8.CF4: history receivers, positive oldest-window timestamp and positive message count are required. Diagnostics print metadata=validated with receiver/non-receiver counts and optional-body presence flags, or metadata=unsupported with a fixed redacted reason. They do not print receiver addresses, message counts, timestamp values, context contents or bot metadata. Unknown fields/wire types and duplicate singletons are refused locally. The supported receiver subset is primary numeric PN/LID; other UserJid kinds remain unsupported locally. Local diagnostic limits are 65536 bytes and 1024 entries per receiver list, not server requirements. Context and bot bodies are opaque and not validated. This metadata check does not implement group/app-data dispatch, authorization or rendering. Metadata values remain redacted; history is not fetched or applied. Poll inspection reports question/option byte lengths and counts, selectable count and secret-presence; it no longer prints question or option text. Unknown nested fields remain visible, and malformed nested protobuf fails inspection. This label does not establish sender authorization, history availability, or synchronization completion. With `inspect: true`, display the plaintext protobuf structure without advancing sessions. With replay_captures, preserved message captures are re-run through inbox::process offline to recover stanzas that an earlier defect refused; this is how the first live group messages were recovered after the sender-key distribution field number was corrected. With --inspect, prekey_pin_matches compares the first pkmsg public identity to saved comparison-direct pins for from, sender_pn, participant and participant_pn aliases. Some(true) means matching, Some(false) means differing, None means no saved pin; invalid_input marks malformed inspection data, and invalid_ciphertext marks a non-byte pkmsg payload. This is offline, read-only, prints no keys or full addresses, does not authenticate the ciphertext and does not authorize a pin replacement. Signal failures report fixed redacted categories rather than underlying address/backend strings. --accept-authenticated-identity-changes requires --replay-captures and conflicts with --inspect. It explicitly selects APK-compatible incoming remote key changes after successful authentication. Previous pins/sessions are archived, an IdentityChanged event is emitted atomically with the inbox/session/prekey commit, and no receipt or network request is sent. Default remains pinned. This is not human verification; no safety-number algorithm is claimed. Group pairwise Signal children from a LID participant select the held LID session; participant_pn identifies a contact alias and does not displace that ratchet. A mapped new pkmsg establishes a LID session; msg retains PN fallback when no LID session exists. An unmapped LID may use a held session. Wrong-session correction recovered the remaining original group capture offline in an isolated store, without network requests or changing the original account. Capture shape inspection now recognizes the exact APK 37.71 group notification type w:gp2 despite its digit. Unknown numeric-containing type values remain redacted as none; the general filter is not widened to expose IDs/addresses. Saved group create/groups_dirty structures remain inspection-only; this label does not apply membership, acknowledge notifications or fetch groups. Newly authenticated SKDM-only group controls use private sender_key_distributed markers without user protobuf; inspection labels the committed key distribution without values or read receipts. It does not parse missing user plaintext, synthesize historical markers or rewind ratchets. These controls dedupe as Duplicate; no new HTTP route is added. Evidence docs/protocol/messaging-transport.md#durable-sender-key-only-group-controls-2026-10-07. --inspect now adds read-only companion_adv diagnostics for one version-2 companion pkmsg and one device-identity child. Status is signatures_verified, missing_device_identity, missing_primary_pin, invalid_primary_pin, ambiguous_input, unsupported_sender, invalid_input or invalid; invalid includes a fixed companion_adv_reason without addresses, keys, ciphertext or ADV bytes. Primary sender paths add no companion result. The primary pin is read only in the actual sender namespace; no alias or companion pin substitutes. Both account and device signatures bind exact signed details and the ciphertext identity, with APK 37.71 E2EE/HOSTED prefixes selected by device type. A supplied account key must match the existing independent pin. Verification does not establish membership, freshness, nested-message authentication, human trust or admission; no pin/session/prekey/event changes or query occur. NON_E2EE and unknown types, missing raw ID/timestamp/key index, duplicate singleton fields and oversized inputs refuse as local supported-subset/parser policy. Library entry point signal::adv::VerifiedDeviceIdentity verifies explicit raw keys or an incoming prekey; signed metadata getters are raw_id, timestamp and key_index. Evidence docs/protocol/peer-identity.md#companion-adv-cryptographic-binding-and-inspection-2026-10-07. Group/status companion version-2 pkmsg now supports the APK 37.71 matched-baseline E2EE branch: both ADV signatures bind the ciphertext identity to an independently held primary; a current independently bound account baseline must have matching raw ID and a verified list timestamp. Old/equal candidates require the actual companion index to match; newer eligible candidates queue expected-timestamp refresh after authentication and may add an absent non-offline device. Nested Signal MAC authentication remains required. The exact companion session/pin, one-time prekey consumption, SKDM and inbox control/message commit together, with transactional rechecks of primary pin, complete list, account identity and login aliases. Pinned versus apk_authenticated incoming policy remains effective; authenticated replacements archive the prior exact companion state. Own PN/LID companions are excluded. Missing own namespace is deferred by a local guard. Absent non-offline newer ADV supports authenticated add-only application; absent/different old/equal index is deleted_device. Refused admission may still allow a held skmsg to decrypt. Offline teardown and raw-ID/type/own-account reconciliation remain unimplemented. Evidence docs/protocol/peer-identity.md#known-companion-prekey-bootstrap-2026-10-07. After signatures_verified, --inspect adds companion_admission with fixed ready, ready_refresh_pending, unsupported_sender, ambiguous_input, missing_device_identity, invalid_device_identity, missing_account, account_changed, own_device, missing_own_identity, missing_primary_pin, invalid_primary_pin, missing_device_list, stale_device_list, unsupported_encryption_type, raw_id_mismatch, missing_list_timestamp, ambiguous_device_membership, invalid_companion_index, conflicting_device_membership, offline_device_update_deferred, pending_device_teardown or deleted_device status. ready describes account-baseline eligibility, not successful nested decryption, human verification or whole-message handling; runtime bootstrap includes direct and group/status known companions. No keys, metadata values or identifiers are emitted. Library companion_admission::inspect is read-only; VerifiedDeviceIdentity::is_e2ee exposes signed type compatibility. Direct ordinary companion pkmsg now uses the same matched-baseline admission and atomic authority checks as group/status. Held non-hosted companion msg uses the exact actual-device ratchet; no PN/LID alias or primary session fallback. Inbox chat/dedupe identity is the actual companion namespace primary (PN or LID), so optional sender_pn changes do not duplicate messages. Events retain the actual device; authenticated PN aliases are saved under the primary LID, never a device-wrapped alias key. Direct SKDM uses the actual companion sender-key namespace. Delivery/read receipts can target the original non-hosted companion PN/LID DeviceJid; explicit primary LID read chats are supported. Incoming policy, own-prekey safeguards, prekey reservations and atomic state checks remain. Full new-device reconciliation is still unfinished. Evidence docs/protocol/peer-identity.md#direct-companion-receive-and-receipts-2026-10-08. Valid signed responses below the expectation retain pending work; reaching responses settle it. Read-only inspection queues nothing. Atomic receive adds only absent actual addresses, preserving held indices and verified timestamp; adv_added_devices records individual ADV provenance until signed address/index confirmation or removal. Complete baseline CAS includes this registry. APK runtime gate parity and reap lifecycle remain incomplete. Static 37.71 evidence identifies ABPropBoolean 35661 with false baked defaults but cached/MobileConfig/preference resolution; the effective value is unknown, so the current removal guard remains a conservative local policy rather than an unconditional server requirement. Evidence docs/protocol/peer-identity.md#companion-removal-property-and-effective-value-2026-10-08. Class whitelist: receipt, notification, message, iq. Type whitelist: delivery, read, played, retry, encrypt, devices, w:gp2, privacy_token, dirty, psa, mex. Echoed IDs, addresses and unknown values remain private. This diagnostic applies no server recovery policy and cannot timestamp a historical content-addressed capture or identify which session produced it. Evidence docs/protocol/terminal-errors.md. Network terminal capture provenance is now saved atomically with the raw capture by the comparison connection: terminal_observation contains first_observed_at/last_observed_at (local Unix milliseconds), last_epoch (actor-local, repeats after restart), observations (saturating count), latest_terminal (latest instrumented terminal commit). Old or offline-only captures report terminal_observation=unknown; offline inspection/replay never backfills provenance. Only stream:error and failure get this metadata, including terminal login replies. Wall clock can move backwards; the latest marker follows commit order, not guessed timestamp ordering. This is local diagnostic metadata, not server fields or globally unique session IDs. Evidence docs/protocol/terminal-errors.md. New ordinary primary LID messages use their actual primary namespace for inbox/event/read lookup even without sender_pn or username. Optional valid phone metadata is saved only after authentication. Existing PN-keyed records remain in place: a bounded lookup requires their original authenticated capture to match the actual primary LID, message ID and original PN alias; ambiguity or missing legacy route evidence refuses locally. Consumed view-once rows with matching original route proof remain duplicates without plaintext restoration or new read queuing. Redelivery never reattributes an event or advances its ratchet. Historical projection and read queuing retain the selected stored key; incoming poll votes can resolve a retained PN poll without changing its original message key. Companion, group and own-peer routes retain their separate guards. No new HTTP route, command, flag, alias guessing, pin adoption or retry/reset authority is introduced. Source and live limits: docs/protocol/peer-identity.md#primary-lid-receive-and-legacy-record-stability-2026-10-09. Incoming reaction keys require present nonempty target ID and a supported parseable remoteJid; malformed/unsupported keys remain opaque. lab-inbox --inspect adds fixed key_validation labels (valid, missing_key, missing_id, invalid_id, missing_remote_jid, invalid_remote_jid, unsupported_remote_jid, malformed_reaction) without printing the key. For primary direct reactions on the sender's own incoming message, original authenticated capture proof retains a historical PN target key while the reacting actor keeps its actual LID. Consumed target records qualify without plaintext restoration; conflicting qualifying rows or missing legacy route evidence refuse locally and atomically. Companion, group and status target reconciliation are not extended by the incoming-target correction. Existing projection markers are preserved. Source and limits: docs/protocol/reactions.md. Capture age diagnostics now use one local timestamp snapshot per inspection; an overflowing age subtraction reports age_s=None instead of panicking. This changes display consistency, not protocol time or server waits. Primary direct reactions to our normal-outbox messages resolve the original immutable chat by unique saved wire ID, either exact primary address or one existing authenticated-lid PN/LID association in either direction. Unattributed/foreign/absent targets retain the envelope namespace. Contact/directory aliases, raw sender_pn alone, companions, groups, status parents and legacy lab-only sends do not supply this association. A reaction never adds acceptance/delivery facts, retries an uncertain send or changes its original ID/progress. Lookup scans all pages and refuses duplicate wire IDs or malformed saved entries with fixed local outbox diagnoses. Source and remaining live limits: docs/protocol/reactions.md#outgoing-intent-attribution-and-quote-scope-2026-10-09. A refused distribution blocks as distribution_refused with the reaction reserved but unsent (uncertain); reaction_distribution_unsupported remains only on older saved preparations.

Supported newly recorded direct/group delivery/read/played facts now preserve valid supplied root t in server_timestamp using signed Java decimal and wrapping milliseconds conversion. Missing/invalid receipt time stays unknown; historical/duplicate facts are not rewritten. First observed fact time is separate from earliest-positive mutable device receipt time. Evidence and live boundary: docs/protocol/receipt-fact-time.md. Direct participant-qualified delivery/read/played receipts now retain the actual device actor only for a matching saved chat and exact immutable original send target; authenticated PN/LID association may join namespaces at the same device ID. Delivery/read/played observations use existing original-target authority and commit as one transaction; malformed input or late saved-state failure commits no partial facts. Inner message_id and per-entry times override root receipt id/type/t in this branch. Unsupported known own/self statuses remain unprojected; the separate key-based participants branch remains unported and cannot fall back to root-id attribution. No original snapshot is backfilled and no resend is authorized. Fresh live aggregate projection remains unverified. post.description: Media routing now has a prospective encrypted refresh wrapper: the explicit lab-transport --media-route operation freezes request bytes/digest/generation/request time and prior applied route, conditionally sends last_id, then atomically stores the original reply, recomputable host projection and current pointer. First-route false and bound non-new replies are supported. Legacy unbound non-new replies still refuse. Refused/unsupported/stale replies preserve evidence without replacing the current object; uploads select that pointer rather than timestamps. No automatic refresh/replay or complete native flight/throttle/cache-restore policy is claimed. Media route expiry now requires preserved requested_at rather than using response receipt time; historical routes lacking request provenance require explicit refresh without automatic query/replay. Pinned APK 2.26.43.72 requires both route ttl and auth_ttl through Java signed-long parsing. Upload route selection now requires both and uses the existing Java-compatible helper; missing/malformed/overflowing lifetimes refuse before reservation. The former missing-auth fallback is removed. Upload HTTP status is persisted as response_headers_received before bounded body streaming; interruption preserves that observation and never authorizes replay. Complete upload validation is still required for uploaded state. See docs/protocol/media-network-outcomes.md. Transmit one selected durable normal-outbox intent through the comparison actor (x-live), or return saved server acceptance without reconnecting. Private MessageRequest uses to for a direct chat or group for an ordinary group, plus stable request_id and text, image (PNG path) or voice_note (Ogg/Opus path). Group uploads are bound to the full group JID. The group actor reserves fresh membership, selected message-context device queries and all missing signed key bundles before staged per-device sender-key distribution and skmsg. Original intent, exact encrypted wire, next ratchets/pins/own sender key, exposure and DeliveryUnknown fact commit together before write. Unknown/refused/partial/omitted/stale preparations do not replay or fall back to cached partial targets. Group and (2026-10-13) direct replies (quote without emoji or quoted_text) with exactly one of text, image or voice_note become quoted outbox intents: group parents are resolved and guarded like other group references, direct parents use the reply command's attribution, and a direct quote whose author is neither the contact nor us is refused; reactions, quoted_text, view_once, fresh_sessions and direct SKDM distribution are explicitly rejected by this JSON path before store/upload access. A quoted image or voice note carries BWx contextInfo (stanzaId, participant, quotedMessage) at media field 17, the field the receive path reads; a reused request ID must keep the same quote target. Evidence docs/protocol/quoted-media.md#sending-2026-10-13; other group message kinds and full own inventory remain unfinished. Group remote bundle replacements honor explicit outgoing_identity_changes=apk_authenticated after signature validation; own identities remain pinned and a changed primary with old companion authority blocks as companion_authority_changed. Previous blocked/unknown preparations are not resumed or reset. Inspect outbox-group-preparations and group key-queries offline. Reusing original accepted JSON returns locally; never create a new ID to repeat an uncertain send. Group receipt output reports partial delivered/read/played device counts, not whole-group or handset confirmation. Existing direct signed-bundle replacement under explicit outgoing_identity_changes=apk_authenticated remains unchanged. The selected CLI wait remains 60 seconds and each actor query has a local 30-second deadline. No live normal group send is established; source and offline/cut-point tests docs/protocol/normal-group-outbox.md. Normal group directory checkpoints are scoped to the immutable local intent ID, so distinct idempotency namespaces cannot share a frozen key plan. Existing foreign/legacy user-request key history blocks rather than being reused or overwritten; inspect original paths. The private-JSON request ID, local intent and final wire ID are never replaced to resend. Normal uploads use image_upload::prepare_outbox for chat binding; the existing comparison image_upload::prepare preserves historical empty-direct-to group bindings and saved uploads. Common direct/pairwise preparation verifies every supplied signed device key bundle even when a saved session exists; a forged same-identity signature refuses locally with invalid signed directory bundle signature before encryption. get.summary: Show queued read, played and retry receipts and their outcomes (offline, redacted)
get.description: Lists the durable receipt queue, including automatic decryption-failure retries. Status is pending, outcome_unknown, server_acknowledged or refused. A retry ACK confirms the request was accepted, not that a replacement message arrived or decrypted. Includes message IDs, but no recipients or message content. Retry reservation and receipt ACK matching now distinguish user/server/agent/device independently of JID wire-encoding kind. New canonical retry reservations first probe all historical encoding-kind selectors atomically; pending, unknown, refused and acknowledged rows keep their selectors, wire and outcomes and block another reservation. Outbound encoding and count-1 once-only policy are unchanged. ACK class/type/message ID and routing qualifiers remain enforced; foreign agent/device/server cannot settle a receipt. Historical duplicate rows are not merged or assigned guessed outcomes. This is a local guard correction; actual live encoding changes and APK internal duplicate policy remain unverified. Evidence docs/protocol/messaging-transport.md#retry-reservation-identity-across-jid-encodings-2026-10-07. New ordinary primary LID messages use their actual primary namespace for inbox/event/read lookup even without sender_pn or username. Optional valid phone metadata is saved only after authentication. Existing PN-keyed records remain in place: a bounded lookup requires their original authenticated capture to match the actual primary LID, message ID and original PN alias; ambiguity or missing legacy route evidence refuses locally. Consumed view-once rows with matching original route proof remain duplicates without plaintext restoration or new read queuing. Redelivery never reattributes an event or advances its ratchet. Historical projection and read queuing retain the selected stored key; incoming poll votes can resolve a retained PN poll without changing its original message key. Companion, group and own-peer routes retain their separate guards. That change added no command, flag, alias guessing, pin adoption or retry/reset authority. Source and live limits: docs/protocol/peer-identity.md#primary-lid-receive-and-legacy-record-stability-2026-10-09. Group read/retry ACKs now require the same participant attribute presence and valid logical participant address as the saved receipt. Incomplete success/error ACKs retain outcome_unknown across restart and never enable replay. Direct ACKs with extra participants remain refused. APK 37.71 Cb1 nullable equality and offline regression evidence: docs/protocol/receipt-ack-correlation.md. That change added no live validation. Offline inspection now rejects missing/invalid saved wire bytes, undecodable wire, non-receipt nodes and absent/non-text/empty IDs with fixed redacted local diagnostics rather than truncating/dropping bytes or showing an empty ID. A malformed row fails the list; no partial result, repair, reservation/status change or replay occurs. Successful response shape is unchanged; x-live=false remains accurate. Evidence docs/protocol/receipt-ack-correlation.md#saved-receipt-inspection-diagnostics-2026-10-09. Outgoing read batching (APK 37.71): reservation groups matching plain read routes into a root ID plus list/item extra IDs, up to the existing sixteen per-message reservation bound. Original per-ID selectors and saved wire bytes stay intact. All selected rows become outcome_unknown atomically before socket writing and never replay after uncertainty. A matching root ACK settles every batch member; extra-ID, wrong-route/type/participant and repeated terminal ACKs cannot settle it. Direct companion destinations and group member devices remain distinct; played/retry and other route metadata stay separate. Queue counts and offline outcomes remain per message ID. Optional encrypted batch_ack_id is ACK correlation only, not another send authority; corrupt correlation returns a fixed diagnostic and rolls back. No new read/read-self policy or route is added. Fresh live multi-ID ACK remains unverified. Evidence docs/protocol/read-receipt-batching.md. Newly queued reads also follow the native to/id/type/participant attribute order; historical saved wire is unchanged. Once-only retry reservations also probe the sender's other PN/LID spelling (same device/agent) from the stanza's sender_pn/sender_lid or participant_pn/participant_lid attributes and the authenticated LID-to-PN mapping, so a redelivery under the other address cannot queue a second retry; an unmapped address without alias attributes remains a separate request, and an invalid saved mapping refuses. Evidence docs/protocol/messaging-transport.md#retry-once-only-across-pn-and-lid-2026-10-13. HTTP (2026-10-13): served read-only by `whatsapp-cli serve --store-routes --token-file <new path>` (experimental-transport build), loopback only, with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; the store is opened per request with the serve process's --store/--account/--key-env, so it answers 503 store_unavailable only while another command (for example listen) holds the store, and 500 store_read_failed for any other read failure; a command starting during a request can fail to open the store and must be rerun. HEAD is also served. The parameters listed here are CLI flags; over HTTP the store comes from the serve process. peer_ticket is an unsalted address hash (guessable for phone numbers); treat responses as account data. Same library call and redacted JSON as the CLI. Disabled store routes answer 404 store_routes_disabled; a missing or wrong token 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer; any query string 400.
