The saved authenticated route retains the actual non-hosted companion PN/LID receipt destination; queued/sent behavior follows this operation and the existing session configuration. Evidence docs/protocol/peer-identity.md#direct-companion-receive-and-receipts-2026-10-08. Incoming group records now include original participant scope. Optional --participant (Receipt.from in the library) selects a PN/LID participant; without it a group/ID pair must identify exactly one saved record. Ambiguity, duplicate historical/canonical claims, or missing original attribution refuse atomically. Group agent selectors are unsupported; direct reads refuse a participant. Original stored routes supply the receipt destination; device/kind variations do not rename logical group messages. Evidence and remaining native-storage unknowns: docs/protocol/group-inbox.md. Outgoing read batching (APK 37.71): reservation groups matching plain read routes into a root ID plus list/item extra IDs, up to the existing sixteen per-message reservation bound. Original per-ID selectors and saved wire bytes stay intact. All selected rows become outcome_unknown atomically before socket writing and never replay after uncertainty. A matching root ACK settles every batch member; extra-ID, wrong-route/type/participant and repeated terminal ACKs cannot settle it. Direct companion destinations and group member devices remain distinct; played/retry and other route metadata stay separate. Queue counts and offline outcomes remain per message ID. Optional encrypted batch_ack_id is ACK correlation only, not another send authority; corrupt correlation returns a fixed diagnostic and rolls back. No new read/read-self policy or route is added. Fresh live multi-ID ACK remains unverified. Evidence docs/protocol/read-receipt-batching.md. Newly queued reads also follow the native to/id/type/participant attribute order; historical saved wire is unchanged.

Store (2026-10-13): no longer creates a missing store; a mistyped path or forgotten --profile fails with "store does not exist" instead of leaving an empty store file. Only registration begin creates one. JSON (2026-10-13): with the global --json flag it prints the saved attempt as redacted JSON (phone and consent secrets replaced by <redacted>, the same as lab-signup status --json), or null without one; --json used to be ignored here.

delete.summary: Discard a completed or blocked attempt (local only)
delete.description: Resets the registration state and discards any completed or blocked attempt. This operation is local only. Since 2026-10-13 reset refuses an attempt created under another profile, so the ordinary CLI cannot discard a lab attempt's refusal and evidence. Exception (2026-10-13, review correction): an attempt from another profile that is blocked with ProfileIncomplete, the local answer of a flow that sends nothing, such as an attempt left by an earlier pinned version, can be reset, if it is not a lab attempt and its history never went past unregistered, preparing and blocked. Evidence docs/protocol/registration-safety-audit.md. Store (2026-10-13): no longer creates a missing store; a mistyped path or forgotten --profile fails with "store does not exist" instead of leaving an empty store file. Only registration begin creates one. An unsent attempt resting unregistered is not reset (it has sent nothing and keeps its keys); resume it with begin.

post.summary: Reconcile an attempt whose request outcome was lost
post.description: Reconciles a registration attempt when the server response was not received locally, by querying the server for the actual status. Store (2026-10-13): no longer creates a missing store; a mistyped path or forgotten --profile fails with "store does not exist" instead of leaving an empty store file. Only registration begin creates one.

post.summary: One comparison-server connection; optional bounded primary login
post.description: Before explicit media-route preparation, recover_throttle validates complete sequenced prospective history and restores missing receipt-anchored waits without replaying requests. It never shortens an existing ambiguous deadline. Active unsequenced507 bounds block preparation without restamping; old unbound rows are counted but remain unreconciled. RecoveryReport exposes only sequenced_receipts, unsequenced_receipts, unbound_records, unbound_active_until, unsequenced_active_until and preserved_until. No automatic query or reset eligibility is inferred. Newly settled media refreshes now receive an atomic positive local settlement_sequence across all outcomes; CLI receipt_order exposes it without raw data. Duplicates preserve order, lost/exhausted counters refuse, and older records remain unsequenced instead of being stamped retrospectively. Historical throttle recovery remains unfinished. Media refresh now preserves code507 positive backoff as a receipt-anchored deadline capped at 10800 seconds; preparation refuses through that deadline without reserving another request. Native-qualified code503 and applied success reset this throttle. Exact duplicate receipts do not extend it. The separate native Fibonacci retry path is not implemented; no automatic retry/query is introduced. throttle_until exposes only the saved numeric deadline. With --media-route, prospective context and applied prior hosts are frozen before the one explicit query; conditional last_id and atomic result projection preserve original wire and refuse stale overwrite. CLI host counts describe the applied projection. No automatic query/retry. See docs/protocol/media-network-outcomes.md#prospective-refresh-integration-2026-11-04. Establish a single connection to the comparison server (x-live) with optional bounded primary login, message transmission, or receive mode. A successful login records this account's own LID from the `<success>` stanza, which a LID-addressed group names us by. When the message JSON carries `group` instead of `to`, the send is a sender-key fan-out: a `w:g2` info query resolves the membership, a `usync devices` query resolves each member's devices, `encrypt` supplies bundles for devices without a session, and one `<message>` carries a per-device `<enc>` distribution inside `<participants>` beside the group `skmsg`. It refuses rather than sending when a member has no device list. After any send the connection is held briefly and whatever the server sends next is preserved, because a recipient that cannot decrypt answers with a `receipt type="retry"` naming the failing device. A `<success>` or `<failure>` login result is preserved too: a `<failure>` carries an `appeal_token` and a refusal cannot be replayed to fetch one again. Receive mode shares listen’s durable once-only decryption-failure retry queue; no repeated count=1 requests after redelivery or uncertain writes. Inspect with receipts (offline). Group pairwise Signal children from a LID participant select the held LID session; participant_pn identifies a contact alias and does not displace that ratchet. A mapped new pkmsg establishes a LID session; msg retains PN fallback when no LID session exists. An unmapped LID may use a held session. Wrong-session correction recovered the remaining original group capture offline in an isolated store, without network requests or changing the original account. When mark_read is enabled, eligible authenticated duplicates recovered offline also enter the once-only read queue on redelivery. The helper checks the saved decrypted readable payload; cleared/consumed rows and protocol-only content are skipped. A write-cut regression verifies uncertain reads are never replayed. Newly reserved comparison group/status sends record exact own sender-key exposure atomically with send/session state. After a supported authenticated remote primary change, indexed own keys rotate on the next new intent, with stale-snapshot checks and encrypted prior-key archival. No acknowledged, refused or uncertain intent is replayed; unindexed historical exposure is unknown and full APK bucket/alias/companion parity remains unfinished. Evidence docs/protocol/cross-device-sync.md#durable-own-sender-key-exposure-and-rotation-2026-10-07. Shared directory bundle parsing now requires one exact user/server/agent/device match, ignores only wire-encoding kind, rejects duplicate requested-user rows or optional one-time keys and contradictory outer errors, while allowing other devices in a batch. These are local ambiguity guards; APK duplicate-reply policy remains unknown. Parsing failure never authorizes pin/session mutation, replay or query reset; peer-keys inspection reports existing invalid_reply. Evidence docs/protocol/peer-identity.md#exact-directory-bundle-selection-2026-10-07. Comparison group sends validate saved membership with offline group_send::recipients_for_group before reserving device-list synchronization: mixed namespaces, wrong own form and absent own membership refuse instead of falling back to raw targets. Initial missing device lists are allowed for this validation; own primary is excluded and remote targets are sorted/deduplicated. The final plan still validates list ownership/companion authority before message reservation. This fixes local routing consistency, not complete APK cached mode/category parity or automatic own-PN selection. No new flag, wire attribute or HTTP route exists; actual live PN send remains unverified. Evidence docs/protocol/groups.md#group-recipient-validation-before-device-sync-2026-10-07. Group/status companion version-2 pkmsg now supports the APK 37.71 matched-baseline E2EE branch: both ADV signatures bind the ciphertext identity to an independently held primary; a current independently bound account baseline must have matching raw ID and a verified list timestamp. Old/equal candidates require the actual companion index to match; newer eligible candidates queue expected-timestamp refresh after authentication and may add an absent non-offline device. Nested Signal MAC authentication remains required. The exact companion session/pin, one-time prekey consumption, SKDM and inbox control/message commit together, with transactional rechecks of primary pin, complete list, account identity and login aliases. Pinned versus apk_authenticated incoming policy remains effective; authenticated replacements archive the prior exact companion state. Own PN/LID companions are excluded. Missing own namespace is deferred by a local guard. Absent non-offline newer ADV supports authenticated add-only application; absent/different old/equal index is deleted_device. Refused admission may still allow a held skmsg to decrypt. Offline teardown and raw-ID/type/own-account reconciliation remain unimplemented. Evidence docs/protocol/peer-identity.md#known-companion-prekey-bootstrap-2026-10-07. Direct ordinary companion pkmsg now uses the same matched-baseline admission and atomic authority checks as group/status. Held non-hosted companion msg uses the exact actual-device ratchet; no PN/LID alias or primary session fallback. Inbox chat/dedupe identity is the actual companion namespace primary (PN or LID), so optional sender_pn changes do not duplicate messages. Events retain the actual device; authenticated PN aliases are saved under the primary LID, never a device-wrapped alias key. Direct SKDM uses the actual companion sender-key namespace. Delivery/read receipts can target the original non-hosted companion PN/LID DeviceJid; explicit primary LID read chats are supported. Incoming policy, own-prekey safeguards, prekey reservations and atomic state checks remain. Full new-device reconciliation is still unfinished. Evidence docs/protocol/peer-identity.md#direct-companion-receive-and-receipts-2026-10-08. Known exact-index newer companion ADV now reports ready_refresh_pending; after nested authentication the atomic receive records expected_timestamp and queues device sync without advancing list_timestamp. Valid signed responses below the expectation retain pending work; reaching responses settle it. Read-only inspection queues nothing. Full new-device reconciliation remains unfinished; live newer-ADV coverage is unverified. Evidence docs/protocol/peer-identity.md#known-companion-newer-adv-refresh-2026-10-08. Remote newer ADV now admits absent non-offline companions or differing held indices after independent account/ADV verification and nested authentication. Atomic receive adds only absent actual addresses, preserving held indices and verified timestamp; adv_added_devices records individual ADV provenance until signed address/index confirmation or removal. Inspection uses ready_refresh_pending without mutation. Local refusals include ambiguous_device_membership, invalid_companion_index, conflicting_device_membership and offline_device_update_deferred. Absent offline senders with unknown removal state are deferred; full teardown lifecycle remains unported; canonical alias/participant/own reconciliation and live new-device validation remain incomplete. Evidence docs/protocol/peer-identity.md#remote-newer-adv-device-application-in-rust-2026-10-08. Namespace-local pending_removed_devices is now recorded atomically by signed reconciliation; nullable legacy state remains unknown, removals persist across reopen, and authenticated returned devices clear markers. Absent offline candidates with known no-marker state may enter authenticated receive; unknown state reports offline_device_update_deferred, marked actual devices pending_device_teardown. Complete baseline CAS includes this registry. Only a first matching text offline attribute parsed as a signed decimal Integer invokes the local guard; malformed/overflow values are null, while zero/negative values qualify. APK runtime gate parity and reap lifecycle remain incomplete. Static 37.71 evidence identifies ABPropBoolean 35661 with false baked defaults but cached/MobileConfig/preference resolution; the effective value is unknown, so the current removal guard remains a conservative local policy rather than an unconditional server requirement. Evidence docs/protocol/peer-identity.md#companion-removal-property-and-effective-value-2026-10-08. Offline parsing is tested against an independent host Java corpus; Android Unicode-version differences and fresh live companion coverage remain unknown. Evidence docs/protocol/peer-identity.md#nullable-offline-companion-metadata-2026-10-08. No keys/history are deleted or requests replayed. Devices inspection exposes the nullable array and optional count. Evidence docs/protocol/peer-identity.md#namespace-local-pending-removal-registry-2026-10-08. Group/status fanout crypto now uses the shared library Snapshot/Prepared pipeline. It retains all original pairwise ratchets even in explicit fresh_sessions mode, stages distributions and skmsg without persistent mutation, and validates every pin/ratchet/own-key/exposure snapshot before committing with the original send reservation. A concurrent late ratchet change refuses instead of overwriting it; fresh mode still enforces pinned identities. Pending identity-triggered own-key rotation preserves the previous generation under the original per-send archive. The subsequent ordinary-group normal outbox adapter and durable directory batches are described in docs/protocol/normal-group-outbox.md; full group parity remains unfinished. Source docs/protocol/group-fanout.md. Prepared retains its secret-bearing bare distribution in zeroizing memory for the existing bounded original-send retry window; it is not printed, returned in a public response or stored unencrypted. Group/status directory-key requests now use durable bounded batches over all frozen devices needing bundles. Reservations precede writes, correlated replies retain exact encrypted wire, complete signed replies assemble locally for shared fanout staging, and unknown/refused/invalid/changed-target/legacy-unattributed outcomes block without resets or automatic query retry. The 32-device query width is local. group key-queries --request-id reports progress offline. Native optional reason=identity, pqsupport and gated context_jid behavior remains unported. Evidence docs/protocol/device-key-batches.md. Routing snapshot correction: group/status planning reads membership, device lists and primary verification pins in one database snapshot. Shared Snapshot::load revalidates every supplied plan field before capturing crypto. Prepared::reserve_in refuses any changed/deleted saved group row, recipient list or primary pin inside the original send transaction, with a fixed redacted local diagnostic and full rollback. Exact-row comparison conservatively includes metadata/timestamps; unrelated contacts do not block. Explicit status audiences remain caller supplied. Complete fanout inspection now also requires current matching saved routing; partial plan counts remain null. No new query, automatic retry, HTTP route or live group verification is established. Evidence docs/protocol/group-fanout.md#routing-snapshot-correction-2026-10-09. Hybrid retry answers (2026-10-13, offline): the post-send group retry answer now derives a native 0x44 hybrid session when the asking device's fresh directory row carries a verified pqkey (library signal::hybrid::selects_pq_key then bundle_for), instead of failing on the classic parser; classic rows are unchanged. No live retry answer is verified. Evidence docs/protocol/hybrid-fanout.md. 2026-10-13: group JSON with image, voice_note or view_once, and any direct-chat quote, are refused before any claim, store or upload (MessageRequest::require_comparison_support); the comparison group path sends text, replies and reactions only and its direct path has no quotes. Both go through outbox-send. Receive gate (2026-10-13, offline): --receive and the lab group-send window check receipt wire content with the same validation as listen; refused content is preserved without ACK and the window continues, while a fault in stored rows still ends it. A status view is recorded only for an accepted receipt. Evidence docs/protocol/replay-safety-audit.md#live-shape-regression-sweep-2026-10-13. Undecodable frames (2026-10-13, offline): the --receive, post-send and group-send windows capture a decrypted frame that does not decode as inbound-undecodable (listed by whatsapp-cli undecodable, epoch null) and continue, as listen does; login, handshake and the bounded reply waits (send ACKs, iq and key replies) still require a decodable frame, which keeps the send or query reserved or uncertain. The group-send window neither correlates nor answers a retry receipt whose content was refused. Startup preflight (2026-11-04, offline): validate config, saved credentials and login payload before endpoint/DNS/TCP/Noise; explicit malformed, non-UTF8 or conflicting saved app versions refuse with redacted errors. Genuine absent legacy fallback remains. No full current-build bootstrap equivalence or ban-prevention guarantee is established. See docs/protocol/network-startup-audit-2026-11-04.md. Server-ping correction (2026-11-04, offline, APK 2.26.43.72): after durable capture and clock observation, an authenticated incoming iq/type=get/xmlns=urn:xmpp:ping receives the native iq/type=result/to=s.whatsapp.net response with no echoed id, xmlns or child. It does not activate the session. Other types/namespaces do not trigger this response; failed writes remain failures and historical captures are not replayed. See docs/protocol/server-pong.md. Noise consistency preflight (2026-11-04, offline): the comparison login derives the Curve25519 public half from the stored private half and refuses a mismatch before endpoint/DNS/TCP/Noise. It preserves both stored halves and creates no login reservation; this does not implement auth-key rotation or authenticate server acceptance. See docs/protocol/authkey-lifecycle.md.

login.description: Send one primary login after certificate verification

receive.description: Preserve incoming stanzas for up to 30 seconds without sending a chat. Incoming `presence` and `chatstate` stanzas are reported (redacted) as they arrive.

media_route.description: Obtain and privately preserve one current media-upload route response

message.description: Private JSON: request_id, either to (direct) or group (`…@g.us` fan-out), and text, image (PNG) or voice_note (Ogg/Opus); a group send is text only so far

recheck_refusal.description: Authorize exactly one further login after a saved `failure`, to tell a temporary limit from a permanent refusal. Requires a saved `failure` (never an ambiguous `outcome_unknown`), refuses to carry a message, and preserves the earlier refusal under its own key instead of overwriting it.

push_name.description: Set the display name others see beside this number: one `<presence name=… type="available"/>` after login (comparison 2.26.37.71 `LX/0y0->A00`, `WriterThread/write/push-name`, confirmed). Fire-and-forget: the server sends no reply, so the CLI reports `written`, not accepted, and records it under the `push-name` checkpoint. The 100-character bound is this client's; the APK enforces none on the wire. Not live-verified yet.

typing.description: Show a typing indicator in this chat (E.164 digits, a phone/LID JID or a `…@g.us` group): announces `presence type=available`, writes `<chatstate to=…><composing/></chatstate>` (`LX/B2G->A01`, confirmed), holds for `typing_seconds` without reading (a cancelled read closes this channel), then writes `<paused/>` (`LX/B2H->handleMessage`, confirmed). Combined with `message`, the indicator runs before the send. Not live-verified yet.

typing_state.description: `recording` is `composing media="audio"` (shown while recording a voice note); `paused` writes only the stop.

subscribe.description: During `receive`, subscribe to these people's availability and typing, as opening their chat does: after activation, `presence type=available`, then per person `<presence type="subscribe" to=…>` with a `<tctoken>` child carrying their saved trusted-contact token when one is held (comparison 2.26.37.71 `LX/0y0->A00`, `WriterThread/write/subscription-request`, confirmed; token bound 1..=120 bytes). Incoming `presence` (available/unavailable, `last` seen) and `chatstate` (composing/recording/paused) are then reported during the window with identities redacted. People only; group typing arrives without a subscription. Not live-verified yet.

get.summary: Classify a saved app-state result offline without applying data
get.description: CLI-only structural inspector over one preserved correlated app-state fetch/patch result. Follows current F2T category precedence: collection error, present version acknowledgement, already-synced, then data. Missing error code uses native -1; version -1 refuses. Consumed data now gets recursive nested-protobuf header preflight: snapshot reference first, every patch parsed before semantic version/exit/mixed-source/duplicate-version checks. Snapshot bytes remain ExternalBlobReference bytes, never downloaded snapshots. JSON prints known names, fixed categories, counts, scalar versions and header outcomes; raw names/text/bodies/reference keys stay private. Native fatal reason metadata is distinct from server error_code; local guard restrictions do not claim native parser parity. Integrity_verified remains false. Successful prospective held fetches additionally expose admission_bound from their sealed admission and exact preserved request/reply in one store read; structural refusal yields false while missing/corrupt admission fails. MACs, key authority and current baseline freshness remain unchecked. Legacy fetches, writes and outer errors have null admission_bound. No state write, download, fetch, reservation, ACK, key installation or missing-store creation. No HTTP route. See docs/protocol/app-state-fetch-completion.md and app-state-structural-headers.md.
get.x-related-settlement: Accepted patch settlement and conflict codes now use the existing Java signed-decimal helper, with exact prepared-version authority and no pure-fetch acknowledgement promotion. Existing correlated 409 patch settlement preflights all selected structural headers and refuses snapshot/external data requiring unsupported retrieval, then retains authenticated decrypted actions encrypted in the same whole-chain transaction as held state and pending release, bound to exact stored request/reply fingerprints. No successful-fetch application or action projection is claimed. See docs/protocol/app-state-catchup-atomicity.md.

parameters.name: action_id
parameters.description: Original saved app-state action identifier

200.description: Redacted structural classification; no integrity or application claim

admission_bound.description: For successful prospective held fetches, checks sealed admission generation/phase, exact original request and preserved reply, then structural binding in one read. False is structural refusal; null is legacy/write/server-error scope. Missing or corrupt required admission fails. Never current baseline equality or MAC verification.

version_ack.description: Native signed acknowledgement scalar; not an applied version

error_code.description: -1 is the absent-code sentinel; no raw server text

snapshot_ref_present.description: Consumed opaque reference body present; not a verified snapshot

has_more_patches.description: Consumed data's literal true flag, otherwise false; null outside data categories

header_status.description: Structural-only preflight result; null when category has no consumed data. Never integrity or application eligibility.

native_header_reason.description: Native F2T fatal reason metadata when established, distinct from server error_code. Local policy failures have null.

failed_patch_index.description: Zero-based index among selected patch children for a native header failure; null for snapshot/local failures or no failure.

header_patch_versions.description: Parsed wire uint64 versions after successful header preflight, never adopted as held state. Empty on failure.

external_mutation_patch_count.description: Count of external-only mutation patches requiring authenticated retrieval; null before successful header preflight.

get.summary: Inspect sealed held-fetch admission and action status offline
get.description: CLI actions --show for the new app-state-held-fetch kind reports admission and numeric action metadata in one consistent read. Phase queued means prepared but never reserved; admitted means reservation provenance exists, not successful result application; locally_refused with baseline_changed leaves the action Queued and unsent. request_digest_matches compares exact stored encoded bytes, not a regenerated Node. Inspection does not recompute current baseline, pending-write or backoff eligibility. Known names/versions only: no raw request/reply, digests, hash/maps, arbitrary server error text or key material. Missing new-kind record, corrupt schema, generation/auth faults are errors, never legacy migration. Legacy version-zero fetch returns no admission record and keeps existing inspection behavior. No state write or HTTP route. See docs/protocol/app-state-held-fetch-admission-design.md.

200.description: Redacted local provenance, not current eligibility or authenticated fetch completion

get.x-local-limitations: No successful fetch application, cursor, snapshot bootstrap, external retrieval or native owner-flight lifecycle is claimed.

get.summary: Inspect saved app-state integrity and logical-index provenance offline
get.description: CLI-only inspection of five validated collection checkpoints. Reports saved version, retained mutation count and whether authenticated logical-index metadata covers all entries. An absent checkpoint has null version and an empty complete state. Legacy nonempty integrity-only rows remain inspectable but require authenticated snapshot reconstruction before incremental verification or construction. Invalid saved maps/hashes refuse. Optional --reconstruct-snapshot PATH --collection NAME loads a bounded local protobuf and reconstructs metadata only when its authenticated version/hash/wire map exactly match an existing held checkpoint and no pending preparation exists. All snapshot keys must already be held; no key is installed. Without flags this is read-only. Neither mode fetches, reserves, resets, applies actions, exposes indexes/MACs or creates a missing store. No HTTP handler is served. See docs/protocol/app-state-logical-index.md. Completeness of logical metadata does not prove native scheduler eligibility or action projection.

get.summary: Inspect the saved server read-receipt preference offline

Native Boolean conversion is true for all/on_standard and false for contacts/none/known/off. This does not change explicit local read or read-self policy, queue a refresh, send traffic, or create a missing store. Current APK 2.26.43.72 evidence in docs/protocol/account-privacy-notifications.md. CLI only; no served HTTP route.

post.summary: Maintain an authenticated comparison connection and process incoming messages
post.description:
Retry-answer metadata correction (2026-11-04, offline): the saved-session and fresh-bundle direct answer paths now put the received retry count unchanged on the enc child as decimal count for supported counts 1 and 2. A devices or prekey-count notification without id (which cannot be acknowledged) is refused the same way, with no device sync or upload, instead of ending the session. A decrypted frame the decoder refuses (for example an unknown token) is stored once, encrypted, as inbound-undecodable:sha256:<digest> with a fixed error class and skipped, instead of ending the session uncaptured; nothing is acknowledged. Nested JID tags in a string position are refused before they are read (they previously recursed until the stack overflowed and aborted the process). An undecodable stream:error or failure (its name read leniently) still ends the session without reconnecting, as does a server close right after a stanza whose name could not be read; the first version had reconnected. Evidence docs/protocol/replay-safety-audit.md#network-input-panic-audit-2026-10-13. A redelivered group view-once already consumed by viewing is a Duplicate and is confirmed. A devices notification naming our own LID no longer queues a contact device sync. Not seen live. Evidence docs/protocol/replay-safety-audit.md#receive-side-audit-2026-10-13. 2026-11-01: a server-ACKed direct send queues our trusted-contact token issue (privacy IQ, kind privacy-token) for that person unless one was scheduled within 182 days (APK HxT.A04 -> GeneratePrivacyTokenJob); the next session transmits it.

Other cases are recorded as `retry-unanswered` with a reason and send nothing. Not live-verified.

Group change notifications (2026-11-01, offline-verified): `w:gp2` add/remove/promote/demote/subject update an existing saved group snapshot before the ACK (2.26.37.71 0yv.A09); other group changes are captured but not applied. Privacy-token ACK correction (2026-11-04, offline, APK 2.26.43.72): unknown token kinds and extra children no longer suppress ACK after supported entries are validated and recorded. Malformed supported entries, invalid sender/metadata and unknown notification types remain refused; this is not a blanket ACK policy. See docs/protocol/network-correctness-audit.md. Server-ping correction (2026-11-04, offline, APK 2.26.43.72): after durable capture and clock observation, an authenticated incoming iq/type=get/xmlns=urn:xmpp:ping receives the native iq/type=result/to=s.whatsapp.net response with no echoed id, xmlns or child. It does not activate the session. Other types/namespaces do not trigger this response; failed writes remain failures and historical captures are not replayed. See docs/protocol/server-pong.md. Noise consistency preflight (2026-11-04, offline): the comparison login derives the Curve25519 public half from the stored private half and refuses a mismatch before endpoint/DNS/TCP/Noise. It preserves both stored halves and creates no login reservation; this does not implement auth-key rotation or authenticate server acceptance. See docs/protocol/authkey-lifecycle.md. Account privacy adoption (2026-11-04, offline): supported server-only account_sync with one non-modify privacy child containing only validated readreceipts categories commits setting and notification deduplication before ACK. Unknown/mixed/modify forms and unowned queued/sent/successful generic privacy setters stay unacknowledged. Store faults remain visible; malformed wire content continues after capture. account-privacy-inspect reads the saved value without policy changes. App-state patch replies now settle the current original action atomically; malformed/stale shape refusals preserve its prepared state and continue receiving. No automatic sync scheduler or refresh is claimed.

post.summary: Request a code or resume an existing attempt; no automatic retries
post.description: Initiates or resumes a registration attempt. Requests a verification code via the specified method (sms or voice). Contacts WhatsApp servers. Not-sent requests (2026-10-13, offline): a request that could not be built (for example a config edited since the attempt froze it) or whose connection failed before any byte was written returns error RequestNotSent and restores the attempt's state before the reservation (a fresh begin returns to unregistered, which the next begin resumes with the same attempt and keys; a resend keeps its pending challenge and method; a submission returns to its challenge; a consent reservation is released; the code-request one-shots, meaning the diagnostics, corrections and resume-preflight, put back the saved request material their reservation replaced, such as a corrected token, and release their latch in the same transaction) instead of recording an unknown outcome. Any other failure may have reached the server and still records outcome_unknown. Review corrections (2026-10-13, offline): once a /v2/exist preflight has been sent in the same step, a later failure records outcome_unknown, never RequestNotSent; the lab transport's own field-patch or encryption failures count as not sent. Evidence docs/protocol/registration-safety-audit.md. Store creation (2026-10-13): begin no longer creates a missing store unless --create-store is given; the refusal names --profile and --create-store. Evidence docs/protocol/registration-safety-audit.md. Store ownership (2026-10-13, review correction): a store records the number it was created for (accounts new and begin --create-store write it). begin on a store that holds no attempt requires that record to name the config's number: an unclaimed store, such as an empty one another command created, needs --create-store, which claims it; another number's store is refused. A store with an attempt is left to the library, which refuses another number's or profile's attempt. Exact restore (2026-10-13, second review): the attempt written back is the exact copy from before the reservation, history included, so a request that never left adds no history and is not counted as a preparation (code_preparation_count, the preflight's client_metrics.attempts). Resume method (2026-10-13): resuming an elapsed cooldown or a first attempt that never left with a method other than the attempt's is refused, naming the saved method; it used to send with the saved method silently. Configured fields.code_bytes.client_metrics for ordinary SMS/voice code requests must be a JSON object; attempts is refreshed from complete saved preparation history (not delivery count), preserving other properties. Malformed metrics or incomplete history refuse before I/O. No metrics field is injected when absent; email_otp and explicit diagnostic overrides keep their existing behavior. Offline verified; delivery improvement is unverified.

create_store.description: Create the store if it does not exist (--create-store). accounts new creates its profile's store, so this is only for a profile made before it did. Without it, a missing store is refused, so a forgotten --profile or a mistyped path cannot create a fresh identity for a number that may already have one. It also claims an unclaimed existing store for the config's number; a store claimed for another number is refused.

Also reports checkpoint_kinds: a count of Checkpoints rows per leading key segment (for example inbound, received, app-state-key, login-identity). Checkpoints holds many unrelated record kinds under one table, so a bare row count cannot answer whether a given kind is present; only the structural prefix is shown, never the JID or digest that follows it. Since 2026-10-13 the kind inbound-undecodable counts decrypted frames listen could not decode; each is kept with its fixed error class for later inspection or re-decoding. whatsapp-cli undecodable lists them, re-checked with the current decoder. Served (2026-10-13) as an opt-in store route: serve --store-routes answers GET /v1/store with the same JSON, under the store bearer token. A checkpoint kind is now printed by name only when it is a lowercase record name ([a-z][a-z0-9_-]*, at most 48 bytes, not hex-like); any other leading segment, for example a key without a ':' separator whose whole text is an address or a digest, is counted under other, for the CLI and the route alike.

post.description: Derives a registration token for the given phone number, generates the master cryptographic key, creates the account profile, and writes a private request configuration with the APK-derived recipe. post.summary: Queue a patch-free app-state fetch offline
post.description: Default queues all five version-zero snapshot requests unchanged. Optional CLI --held freezes existing validated collection checkpoints into a distinct app-state-held-fetch action and sealed preparation in one transaction; repeatable --collection selects a subset, otherwise every collection must exist. No missing checkpoint is inferred empty. Held mode requests actual held versions with no snapshot flag, installs no keys and enforces known explicit backoff/pending-write guards. Reservation rechecks generation, exact stored wire SHA-256, full canonical baseline and ownership before atomically marking admission plus Sent. A changed baseline becomes a permanent local refusal with action still Queued; no request rebuild, nonce/key rotation or fake server error. Pending writes/backoff defer without changing the phase; unrelated actions can proceed. actions --show ID prints atomic redacted admission/status metadata; inspection does not recompute current eligibility. Legacy fetches receive no retrospective admission. Successful fetch application, authenticated mutation cursor/held-state commits, external downloads, native scheduler ownership and continuation remain incomplete. Historical empty sync does not prove an account has no app state. Both fetch kinds use preserved receipt-time outer-error backoff; no sent action is retried. No HTTP route. See docs/protocol/app-state-held-fetch-admission-design.md.

post.summary: Queue an app-state contactAction patch publishing every saved contact (offline; a session transmits it)
post.description: Build and queue a SyncdPatch of contactAction SET mutations, one per saved contact, into the critical_unblock_low collection (LX/Azs->A00 routes contactAction there, confirmed — not a 'regular' collection). Index is ["contact", <jid>] and SyncActionData.version is 2, both confirmed from LX/B6M. Mints this device's app-state key if it has none. The <collection version> attribute is the version the client currently holds and is omitted for a never-synced collection (confirmed, CSe.A01 call sites). LIVE STATUS: refused. Two attempts, both answered iq type=error code=400 text=bad-request; the second carried the corrected version semantics. Not iterated further. See docs/protocol/chat-actions.md for the undistinguished candidates. Atomic patch lifecycle (2026-11-04, offline): key selection, baseline, original action wire and prepared state commit together, with one unsettled patch per collection. Invalid stored-key errors no longer trigger generation fallback. Socket reservation revalidates original wire/held state and blocks missing/corrupt preparation. Only a matching original collection and accepted version promote state, with baseline comparison and MAC verification; malformed/stale outcomes retain preparation. Legacy prepared rows reverify from immutable original wire. Conflict-chain application and pending release share a transaction; no partial advancement or retry. See docs/protocol/app-state-patch-atomicity.md. Explicit app-state backoff (2026-11-04, offline): a valid outer-error backoff persists from original reply receipt time. New patches are blocked until its deadline; never-sent queued patches defer while unrelated controls may drain. Expiration uses the same original request once, not a retry of any sent action. Invalid/overflowing hints preserve pending state. Full native scheduling and nested retry classification remain unported.

post.summary: Ask for a new code on the attempt already in progress
post.description: Re-request the verification code for a registration attempt that is already in a pending challenge, because a delivered code expires long before the attempt does. Keeps the attempt id, its identity, its keys and its history; creates no new attempt; honours the challenge handle's retry_after; and refuses any other state except the saved stale refusal described below. This is the official client's resend, not a restart. Not-sent requests (2026-10-13, offline): a request that could not be built (for example a config edited since the attempt froze it) or whose connection failed before any byte was written returns error RequestNotSent and restores the attempt's state before the reservation (a fresh begin returns to unregistered, which the next begin resumes with the same attempt and keys; a resend keeps its pending challenge and method; a submission returns to its challenge; a consent reservation is released; the code-request one-shots, meaning the diagnostics, corrections and resume-preflight, put back the saved request material their reservation replaced, such as a corrected token, and release their latch in the same transaction) instead of recording an unknown outcome. Any other failure may have reached the server and still records outcome_unknown. Review corrections (2026-10-13, offline): once a /v2/exist preflight has been sent in the same step, a later failure records outcome_unknown, never RequestNotSent; the lab transport's own field-patch or encryption failures count as not sent. Evidence docs/protocol/registration-safety-audit.md. Exact restore (2026-10-13, second review): the attempt written back is the exact copy from before the reservation, history included, so a request that never left adds no history and is not counted as a preparation (code_preparation_count, the preflight's client_metrics.attempts). Also accepts an attempt saved as blocked by a /v2/register `stale` (expired code) refusal, honouring its saved wait. Since 2026-11-01 `stale` no longer blocks: verify-code returns to code entry on a new step (2.26.37.71 VerifyPhoneNumber.A5O case 9 forgets the stored code, clears the input and stays on code entry), so a resend follows. Other refusals still refuse. 2026-11-01: `incorrect` and `mismatch` refusals of a code also return to code entry (2.26.37.71 VerifyPhoneNumber.A5O default branch and A1v); a `mismatch` gates the next code for retry_after or 60 s (answer_not_before) without consuming the step, and resend-code accepts attempts saved as blocked by either. Configured fields.code_bytes.client_metrics for ordinary SMS/voice code requests must be a JSON object; attempts is refreshed from complete saved preparation history (not delivery count), preserving other properties. Malformed metrics or incomplete history refuse before I/O. No metrics field is injected when absent; email_otp and explicit diagnostic overrides keep their existing behavior. Offline verified; delivery improvement is unverified.

get.summary: List who has received, viewed, played or liked our statuses
get.description: Offline. Lists the recorded status receipts and likes: who reported, for which status, and how far they got (delivered, read, played), plus any reactions. Receipts are kept at the furthest state a viewer reached, so a delivery replayed from an offline queue cannot demote a view. Reading this sends nothing and emits no read receipt. Status likes require the status@broadcast singleton (zero agent/device), rather than any broadcast-domain reaction key. Other broadcasts, malformed keys and companion-suffixed status targets do not become status likes. Static APK 37.71 BoQ.A00/8oR evidence and local limits: docs/protocol/reactions.md. Recording correction (2026-10-13, offline): only the entry-less participants message_id receipt observed live is a status view; from 2026-10-10 until this correction it was refused as an empty aggregate and ended listen, so views received in that window may be missing. An aggregate with entries is a chat receipt, not a view. Evidence docs/protocol/status.md#views-status-receipts-observed-2026-09-24.

Each child is included only when supplied, so setting a PIN cannot clear the recovery address as a side effect, and an empty code turns two-step verification off. The PIN is read from redirected stdin, never a command-line argument, and is never echoed or logged. Distinct from `lab-signup verify-pin`, which answers a PIN challenge rather than changing the PIN. Builds on the collection state the server last accepted and promotes the new state only once the server accepts it; a 409 conflict is caught up from the returned patches. A wait or unsettled patch refuses locally before another patch or presence is queued. See docs/protocol/app-state-patch-atomicity.md.

These observations are unauthenticated: they do not establish a legitimate identity change, replace a pin, advance a session, clear verification, or authorize sending. The peer address is represented by a local SHA-256 selector. Replay/redelivery of the same peer/pinned/observed combination preserves the original timestamp. HEAD is also served. The parameters listed here are CLI flags; over HTTP the store comes from the serve process. peer_ticket is an unsalted address hash (guessable for phone numbers); treat responses as account data. Same library call and redacted JSON as the CLI. Disabled store routes answer 404 store_routes_disabled; a missing or wrong token 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer; any query string 400 (CLI-only options are not served).

get.summary: Inspect saved peer pins, sessions and retained-device key coverage (offline)
get.description: Reads one logical snapshot without queries, key replacement or sends. Requires a primary phone-number chat JID. Returns hashed peer selectors, diagnostic public-key fingerprints, held-session/pin agreement, and all authenticated primary LID mappings. A qualifying saved incoming transition establishes local provenance only; it is not a WhatsApp safety number or human verification. Store opening can commit engine metadata; protocol records are inspected read-only. No HTTP route is implemented. Also reports nullable retained E2EE device-key coverage in that snapshot: retained/pinned counts, hashed missing-pin selectors, saved signed-list status, skipped-hosted count and notification-hash agreement. A primary-only fallback or fully pinned retained set does not establish complete current APK fingerprint inventory, selected scheme or human verification. Invalid saved pins/device-list consistency are local diagnostics. No safety number is computed. Reports nullable local verification metadata: verified bit, action sequence and identity/pin agreement. This human claim is distinct from authenticated transition provenance. Saved device_key_coverage additionally exposes nullable device_authority (binding_known, primary_pin_present, primary_pin_matches and companions_current), recomputed read-only against the exact current primary namespace pin. Historical companions_verified does not prove current signer authority; the private binding fingerprint is not exported. No PN/LID alias is inferred. Evidence docs/protocol/cross-device-sync.md#signed-device-authority-and-authenticated-refresh-2026-10-07. Also reports pending_sender_key_rotations for each exact primary namespace. Authenticated supported primary changes mark indexed own exposed keys in the existing transaction; the next newly reserved comparison group/status send mints a fresh key. Existing uncertain/refused sends are never replayed, incoming chains are retained, and historical unindexed distributions remain unknown. This is a local supported subset, not full APK bucket/actor or PN/LID migration parity. Evidence docs/protocol/cross-device-sync.md#durable-own-sender-key-exposure-and-rotation-2026-10-07. Primary-change follow-ups now compare validated agent-0/device-0 user or LID primaries independently of wire-encoding kind: indexed own sender-key rotations and remote device refresh stay scoped, while own PN/LID identities remain excluded. Rotation inspection ignores encoding kind but preserves agent/device and namespace. No historical exposure is inferred, send replayed or identity adopted by inspection. Offline PN incoming/LID signed-bundle archive and own exclusion regressions cover the local correction; live alternate primary encoding remains unverified. Evidence docs/protocol/cross-device-sync.md#encoding-independent-primary-change-follow-ups-2026-10-07. Static APK 2.26.37.71 D4x receipt/version/privacy-token side effects are documented separately in docs/protocol/identity-receipts.md. Native receipt-device caches, primary_device_version and privacy refresh job lifecycle are not reported as implemented by this inspector. Current receipt-outbox ACK/uncertainty reservations are a different durable model and remain preserved. The new 23-topic/53-declaration evidence bundle introduces no runtime cleanup, counter, token fabrication, key adoption, retry or HTTP route. PeerPinState now exposes primary_device_version from tracked authenticated primary replacements. Missing historical state remains null; no backfill, alias merge, receipt reset or request is inferred. See docs/protocol/primary-device-version.md. Requires a nonempty peer user in addition to the primary PN namespace/components; server-only destinations refuse locally before store access. The peer-key normal/refresh queue and directory/pin inspection share this prerequisite. Fixed local diagnostic: requires a nonempty peer user; server-only JID is not a peer. Offline regression preserves stored pins/sessions and uncertain query reservations across reopen. No new HTTP route or live validation. Evidence: docs/protocol/peer-identity.md#empty-peer-guard-on-key-queries-and-pin-inspection-2026-10-09.

post.summary: Queue or inspect one peer directory key query (offline)
post.description: peer-keys queues a normal encrypt/key IQ on the existing once-only action queue; listen transmits it over authenticated Noise. Repeated queueing returns the original action ID locally. --show inspects the latest saved result and current PN/LID pin matches without adopting a key, deriving a session or sending a chat. --refresh is explicit and permitted only after a successful valid signed prior bundle; all old replies remain encrypted. Queued, uncertain, refused, invalid and missing prior queries cannot be refreshed. Output omits peer addresses, public key bytes and raw server error text. Fingerprints are SHA-256 diagnostics, not safety numbers or human verification. This is CLI-only; no HTTP route exists. This full prekey-bundle query does not implement APK 37.71 encrypt/identity recovery after ADV verification failure; peer-identity-query now stages that distinct read without adopting keys; automatic recovery/application remains unfinished. See docs/protocol/cross-device-sync.md#adv-identity-follow-up-and-raw-id-cleanup-2026-10-07. Shared directory bundle parsing now requires one exact user/server/agent/device match, ignores only wire-encoding kind, rejects duplicate requested-user rows or optional one-time keys and contradictory outer errors, while allowing other devices in a batch. These are local ambiguity guards; APK duplicate-reply policy remains unknown. Parsing failure never authorizes pin/session mutation, replay or query reset; peer-keys inspection reports existing invalid_reply. Evidence docs/protocol/peer-identity.md#exact-directory-bundle-selection-2026-10-07. Primary address correlation now compares exact user/server/agent/device components across supported Plain and AD_JID encodings, rather than comparing JidKind as an identity. Zero-component AD_JID is a primary wire encoding; unrelated PN/LID/hosted namespaces, users, agents and companions remain distinct. Unsupported FB/interop kinds are refused locally before queueing. post.summary: Compute native fingerprint display from explicit inputs (offline)
post.description: CLI only; no HTTP route. Does not open the account store, fetch keys, compare QR data, select the active APK scheme, or commit human verification. Reads a private regular JSON file <=64 KiB with local/remote sides (FingerprintDisplayInput). Rejects unknown fields; error text omits offending values. Raw keys are sorted unsigned, serialized with 0x05, concatenated without deduplication and hashed using APK 37.71 native 5200-round identifier-bound SHA-512. Six big-endian five-byte groups yield 30 digits per side, with lexical join to 60. Native-display fixtures use actual ARM64 hash control flow with host-modeled SHA/MCF; whole native display and live comparison are not established. Complete device inventory and scheme selection remain caller responsibilities. Output contains no input identifier or public key. Resource bounds are client policy. See docs/protocol/safety-number.md. Optional --qr-version 0|1 plus --qr-output exports APK-derived native V4 combined fingerprint protobuf to a new private mode-600 binary file, without opening account storage. V4 QR needs full plain-primary lid_jid matching display_identifier and at least PN or username presence on each side. Optional QR-specific fields are ignored for display-only calculations. V4 local PN is suppressed with a present username; remote PN retained. Version 1 uses H(K,K), not identifier-bound display hash. Full identifiers and key/hash material appear in the private export, never stdout. Refuses existing output or invalid inputs before export; partial write failures preserve the private artifact. No QR image rendering, scan, peer comparison, active scheme/inventory assertion or verification commit. Independent literal-tag wire fixtures use host-modeled-SHA actual ARM64 hash flow for digests; full native serialization and live scan remain unverified. Explicit --qr-scheme native-v3 selects V3 binary export (omitting it preserves native-v4). This flag requires qr-version/qr-output. V3 retains both PN fields despite username presence; optional LID supports the traced numeric-primary subset and zero-device suffixes, whose supplied full text is retained. V3 display/export requires pn_identifier equal to display_identifier on each side: a conservative CLI subset based on native stable-PN display, not a server rule. Library encode_v3 also supports LID-only explicit inputs without displaying. Independent V3 literal-wire fixtures cover versions 0/1, both addresses, PN-only, LID-only, zero suffix, optional presence and export/compare orientation. Static native serializer trace confirms fields/order; full native pack/JNI/current inventory and live scanning remain unverified.

get.description: Offline counts-only inspection of the encrypted RefreshOutcome for an existing group-refresh action ID. Historical reports lacking continuation metadata default to no automatic continuation. Mixed/outcome and continuation behavior is offline tested, not live verified. HTTP (2026-10-13): served read-only by `whatsapp-cli serve --store-routes --token-file <new path>` (experimental-transport build), loopback only, with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; the store is opened per request with the serve process's --store/--account/--key-env, so it answers 503 store_unavailable only while another command (for example listen) holds the store, and 500 store_read_failed for any other read failure; a command starting during a request can fail to open the store and must be rerun. HEAD is also served. Same library call and redacted JSON as the CLI. Disabled store routes answer 404 store_routes_disabled; a missing or wrong token 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer. Over HTTP the store comes from the serve process and the only accepted query is exactly id=<action id>, unencoded, satisfying the library ID rule (ASCII alphanumerics and -_.:, at most 128 bytes); a missing, renamed, repeated, empty, percent-encoded or additional parameter answers 400 before the store opens. An unknown id answers 200 null. Group addresses and sizes are not in the response; next_action is a local action ID. The other parameters listed here (store, account, key environment, profile, profiles directory) are CLI flags; over HTTP the store comes from the serve process and any of them is an extra query parameter, answered 400.
